**[00:18:53.520] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-000177)

**[00:19:21.420] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-000179)

**[00:19:23.520] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-000180)

**[00:19:33.740] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-000182)

**[00:19:41.720] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-000183)

**[00:19:53.520] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-000185)

**[00:19:54.760] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-000186)

**[00:20:07.900] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-000188)

**[00:20:22.300] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-000189)  
Hindi tayo titigil sa pagsulong at patuloy na pagpapalawig ng mas komprehensibong benefit packages, hindi lamang para sa higit ng mga nangangailangan, kundi pati na rin sa mga mga gawa at middle-class families na regular na naguhulog, ngunit maaari pa rin mabaon sa gastusin kapag tinamaan ng malubhang karamdaman.

**[00:20:47.780] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-000190)

**[00:30:45.920] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-000435)

**[00:30:49.740] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-000436)

**[00:30:50.740] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-000437)  
Governor Remolona, you may proceed.

**[00:30:53.520] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000438)  
Honorable Senate President Win Gatchalian,

**[00:30:56.900] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000439)  
thank you for this opportunity to brief you,

**[00:31:00.000] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000440)  
on the macroeconomic outlook to provide context for the Fiscal Year 2027 budget.

**[00:31:08.360] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000441)  
As the country's central bank, our primary mandate is to safeguard price stability.

**[00:31:15.940] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000442)  
This mandate recognizes the fact that low inflation provides a sound foundation

**[00:31:23.440] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000443)  
for sustained economic growth and job creation.

**[00:31:28.860] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000444)  
At the DBCC, we have a number of issues.

**[00:31:29.800] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000445)  
In the DBCC briefing in Congress last week, I said that we worry a lot about inflation.

**[00:31:37.200] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000446)  
We know how inflation affects the purchasing power of Filipino families.

**[00:31:43.220] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000447)  
Indeed, surveys say that in people's minds,

**[00:31:47.180] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000448)  
inflation is the leading indicator of their well-being.

**[00:31:53.710] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000449)  
The main challenge we now face with regard to inflation is global supply shocks.

**[00:32:01.750] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000451)  
Since the start of the war in Iran, oil prices have risen sharply.

**[00:32:06.370] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000452)  
As a consequence, our energy prices and our food prices went through the roof.

**[00:32:14.250] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000453)  
There is little the BSP can do about the price of oil itself, because our tools are limited

**[00:32:23.790] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000454)  
to those coming from the supply side.

**[00:32:26.310] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000455)  
With that limitation, we must focus on the second round effects of global supply shocks.

**[00:32:31.070] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000456)  
To address inflation pressures, the BSP has already tightened monetary policy twice this year.

**[00:32:42.030] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000457)  
These actions were carefully calibrated to help push inflation back towards our target

**[00:32:49.290] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000458)  
and to keep inflation expectations well anchored,

**[00:32:53.630] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000459)  
while at the same time recognizing the current weakness in economic activity.

**[00:33:01.300] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000460)  
While at the same time recognizing the current weakness in economic activity, recent data on inflation is much more punctual than any other recent videos.

**[00:33:02.560] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000462)  
have been somewhat encouraging. Inflation has moderated in recent months, although it remains

**[00:33:09.560] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000463)  
well above our target of 3%. Looking ahead, we expect inflation to gradually move closer

**[00:33:18.550] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000464)  
to our target over the medium term. At the same time, we remain vigilant about the continued risks

**[00:33:26.830] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000465)  
to the inflation outlook. The Monetary Board stands ready to take the necessary measures

**[00:33:33.890] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000466)  
to fulfill our mandate. We also have a mandate for financial stability.

**[00:33:41.790] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000467)  
In this regard, I am pleased to inform that the Philippine banking system remains strong

**[00:33:48.790] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000468)  
and resilient. Banks continue to be well capitalized, adequately provisioned,

**[00:33:55.750] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000469)  
and supported by ample liquidity. Together with the country's solid external position,

**[00:34:03.290] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000470)  
these strengths will continue to improve.

**[00:34:03.890] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000471)  
These strengths provide important buffers against global challenges and uncertainties.

**[00:34:11.230] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000472)  
Overall, these developments support the macroeconomic assumptions

**[00:34:14.810] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000473)  
that underpin the proposed fiscal year 2027 national budget.

**[00:34:22.470] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000474)  
With that, let me turn the floor over to Deputy Governor Zeno Abenoa,

**[00:34:27.350] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000475)  
who will present a more detailed discussion of recent economic developments and macroeconomic

**[00:34:33.790] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000476)  
assumptions. Maraming salamat po.

**[00:34:33.890] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-000477)  
Thank you, Governor Remolona. Next, we'd like to call our Secretary.

**[00:34:45.895] Senator Vicente C. Sotto III** (asr-000477-split-2)  
Mr. Chairman. Yeah, Mr. Chairman.

**[00:34:51.898] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-000477-split-2-split-2)  
Yes, Senate President...

**[00:34:54.899] Senator Vicente C. Sotto III** (asr-000477-split-2-split-2-split-2)  
I think the BSP wants to continue with the presentation.

**[00:34:57.900] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-000478)  
Who will make the presentation?

**[00:35:00.580] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-000479)  
Dep Gov Abenoja.

**[00:35:01.660] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-000480)  
Okay

**[00:35:01.840] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-000481)  
please proceed.

**[00:35:03.320] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000482)  
Thank you, Mr. Chair.

**[00:35:05.620] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000483)  
I join the Governor in thanking and greeting good morning to our Senate President,

**[00:35:12.800] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000484)  
Win Gatchalian, our Chair of the Committee on Finance, Senator J.V. Ejercito,

**[00:35:20.020] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000485)  
our Honorable Vice Chairpersons, and Senators.

**[00:35:26.140] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000486)  
For the next few minutes, I will be providing a background, particularly our recent assessment

**[00:35:32.720] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000487)  
on the monetary, financial,

**[00:35:35.320] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000491)  
and external sector performance of the country.

**[00:35:38.280] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000492)  
And this will provide some background to the macroeconomic assumptions that have been reflected

**[00:35:44.040] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000493)  
when the 2027 budget has been formulated.

**[00:35:49.440] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000494)  
So let me start with inflation.

**[00:35:52.760] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000495)  
Here we show the inflation numbers.

**[00:35:56.100] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000496)  
The target for the inflation is an average of 3% every year.

**[00:36:01.960] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000497)  
And if you look back last year in 2025,

**[00:36:05.040] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000498)  
we see here that inflation, for the most part, has been manageable.

**[00:36:09.800] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000499)  
In fact, it's been below that 3% inflation target.

**[00:36:14.060] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000500)  
And this is due particularly to the benign food inflation and energy prices last year.

**[00:36:23.280] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000501)  
And this continued, these favorable inflation numbers continued during the first two months of 2026.

**[00:36:30.360] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000502)  
However, the conflict in the Middle East since February,

**[00:36:34.360] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000503)  
and February, 2026, drove global oil prices higher.

**[00:36:38.740] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000504)  
And this translated to significant spillover to domestic inflation.

**[00:36:44.160] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000505)  
As we can see, the inflation rapidly rose from 2.4% in February.

**[00:36:50.120] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000506)  
It went to as high as 7.2% back in April.

**[00:36:56.300] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000507)  
But since then, it has gradually eased to 6.2% as of July of this year.

**[00:37:04.360] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000508)  
However, inflation continues to be well above the target of 3%,

**[00:37:10.180] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000509)  
despite that moderation in the last three or four months.

**[00:37:15.180] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000510)  
The moderation that we have seen since the period,

**[00:37:18.100] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000511)  
during the period May to July months,

**[00:37:22.440] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000512)  
reflects, for the most part, lower global oil prices,

**[00:37:27.460] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000513)  
as well as some improvement in food supply.

**[00:37:30.900] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000514)  
Now, what was the response of the B2B?

**[00:37:34.360] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000515)  
What was the response of the B2B to this recent developments?

**[00:37:38.720] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000516)  
For the B2B, the monetary policy shifted to a tightening stance,

**[00:37:44.620] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000517)  
given the uptick in inflation and the increase in the inflation outlook.

**[00:37:51.160] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000518)  
The B2B decided to raise target policy rates from 4.25% by 25 basis points each,

**[00:37:59.600] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000519)  
last April and again in June 2026.

**[00:38:04.360] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000520)  
This brings the policy rate to 4.75%.

**[00:38:08.460] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000521)  
Let me just note that, as mentioned by our committee chair and the governor,

**[00:38:14.860] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000522)  
the BSP Monetary Board will be meeting today, again, to assess monetary policy.

**[00:38:23.420] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000523)  
But we are constrained to speak about the decision until the announcement at 2.30 this afternoon.

**[00:38:33.480] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000524)  
Now,

**[00:38:34.360] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000525)  
describing what we have done in the past, in the last two policy meetings,

**[00:38:39.500] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000526)  
we characterize this as a calibrated move by the BSP.

**[00:38:44.240] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000527)  
And the main purpose is really to anchor inflation expectations

**[00:38:49.700] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000528)  
and reduce what we call spillover or second-round effects

**[00:38:54.140] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000529)  
that could bring about a broader price pressure moving forward.

**[00:39:01.160] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000530)  
But equally important, and we highlight here,

**[00:39:03.920] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000531)  
Mr. Chair, is that this policy action, this measured policy action,

**[00:39:09.840] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000532)  
is meant also to complement fiscal measures so that it can support the steady consumption

**[00:39:16.560] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000533)  
and strengthening of business sentiment moving forward.

**[00:39:22.300] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000534)  
If you look at the policy environment right now,

**[00:39:25.280] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000535)  
we are indeed in a very challenging external environment.

**[00:39:28.980] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000536)  
And the BSP will remain data dependent.

**[00:39:32.800] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000537)  
The BSP will remain vigilant

**[00:39:34.340] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000542)  
And is prepared to take further monetary policy actions

**[00:39:37.840] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000543)  
to ensure that inflation returns to the 3% target over the medium term.

**[00:39:44.700] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000544)  
So where do we see inflation moving forward?

**[00:39:49.380] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000545)  
Here, Mr. Chair, we showed the forecast, the outlook for inflation,

**[00:39:53.980] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000546)  
that we did in the last policy meeting back in June 18 of this year.

**[00:39:59.640] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000547)  
And this outlook will be updated this afternoon.

**[00:40:02.300] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000548)  
And there will be announcements.

**[00:40:03.820] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000549)  
But just for recall, what we are seeing back in the last policy meeting

**[00:40:09.560] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000550)  
is that for 2026, inflation could average 6.4% this year.

**[00:40:16.280] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000551)  
Next year, 4.5%.

**[00:40:18.180] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000552)  
And then in 2028, 3.1%.

**[00:40:21.880] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000553)  
So it could take a little bit of time before we see inflation going back again

**[00:40:28.000] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000554)  
or averaging again close to the target of 3%.

**[00:40:33.820] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000555)  
At the same time, we emphasize another measure of inflation.

**[00:40:39.580] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000556)  
And this is what we call the core inflation.

**[00:40:42.360] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000557)  
Core inflation is a measure of the underlying price pressure.

**[00:40:49.560] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000558)  
And it is something that is more lasting, more stable

**[00:40:53.300] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000559)  
in affecting the price dynamics in the economy.

**[00:40:58.680] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000560)  
And this is something that we also closely monitor.

**[00:41:02.240] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000561)  
What are some of the upside risks that we are looking at?

**[00:41:07.500] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000562)  
There are several risks, and they could emanate from the higher

**[00:41:11.920] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000563)  
or elevated global oil prices, this anchoring of inflation expectations,

**[00:41:18.360] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000564)  
as well as some impact, especially in the near term,

**[00:41:22.620] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000565)  
coming from weather disturbances.

**[00:41:25.840] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000566)  
Now, if you look at the private sector surveys on their inflation forecast,

**[00:41:31.180] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000567)  
they also point.

**[00:41:32.240] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000568)  
to higher inflation over the near term.

**[00:41:35.400] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000569)  
But their expectation is that inflation could indeed come back

**[00:41:40.300] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000570)  
to close to the target by 2028.

**[00:41:44.680] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000571)  
Now, going to the banking system, how is the banking system performing?

**[00:41:49.740] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000572)  
The Philippine banking system remains healthy and supported by strong fundamentals.

**[00:41:56.920] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000573)  
In our oversight in supervising the banking sector,

**[00:42:00.800] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000574)  
the BSP,

**[00:42:02.240] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000575)  
we emphasize risk-based, forward-looking, and systemic risk-focused bank supervision.

**[00:42:10.680] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000576)  
This is important so that we can help ensure that banks sustain their growth in assets

**[00:42:16.480] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000577)  
and deposits, as well as continued profitability.

**[00:42:21.360] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000578)  
Looking across different metrics, for example, those on capital adequacy, on liquidity,

**[00:42:27.900] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000579)  
they all remain well above international norms.

**[00:42:32.240] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000580)  
If you look at non-performing loans, they also continue to be manageable,

**[00:42:37.240] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000581)  
and the banks are well provisioned against this non-performing portion of their loan book.

**[00:42:43.560] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000582)  
Looking ahead, we think that the banking system is well positioned to support economic activity

**[00:42:51.360] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000583)  
and financial stability.

**[00:42:54.680] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000584)  
An important element of the financial system is to provide efficient services

**[00:43:00.920] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000585)  
to our banks.

**[00:43:02.520] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000586)  
And from an economic perspective, we want to ensure we can support the değilism of both

**[00:43:07.400] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000587)  
households and businesses.

**[00:43:10.260] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000588)  
And here we show some of the developments in terms of access to financial services.

**[00:43:16.920] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000589)  
The chart on the left shows the digital payments reach almost 65% of retail transactions

**[00:43:24.960] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000590)  
by volume last year.

**[00:43:28.300] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000591)  
This surpasses the targets of 50% up to 54%

**[00:43:32.100] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000592)  
What this highlights is that there's a continued momentum in the adoption of electronic payment channels in the country.

**[00:43:42.380] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000593)  
But again, there's also an important element into this growing digital payment system in our economy.

**[00:43:49.880] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000594)  
And this refers to what are called network externalities.

**[00:43:54.220] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000595)  
This means that the value and convenience of our domestic payment system, our domestic electronic payment channels, increases as more consumers, more merchants, and more financial institutions participate in this financial ecosystem.

**[00:44:13.460] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000596)  
And this is something that the BSP has been promoting.

**[00:44:17.200] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000597)  
On the right side, we show the increasing number of bank deposit accounts.

**[00:44:21.720] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000598)  
It has reached over 28 million.

**[00:44:24.220] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000599)  
It has reached over 28 million accounts as of March 2026, with more than 170 banks offering basic deposit accounts.

**[00:44:34.220] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000600)  
These are no-frills deposit accounts, and it would help financial inclusion in our country.

**[00:44:43.600] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000601)  
This is an important priority of the BSP.

**[00:44:46.820] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000602)  
We also welcome the recent announcements of several banks to reduce or waive interbank digital transaction fees.

**[00:44:55.920] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000604)  
This makes it more affordable and accessible for Filipino households.

**[00:44:59.980] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000605)  
as

**[00:45:00.000] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000606)  
well as small businesses to access convenience of electronic fund

**[00:45:05.760] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000607)  
transfers. We also thank our legislators for the passage of an important law and

**[00:45:12.720] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000608)  
we refer here to the anti-financial account scamming up. This is indeed a

**[00:45:19.180] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000609)  
vital legislation to continue to improve consumer protection to do stronger

**[00:45:25.420] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000610)  
safeguards for fraud and faster complaint resolution. This is important

**[00:45:31.360] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000611)  
support as we try to grow, expand our financial system, not only to the

**[00:45:37.080] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000612)  
traditional banks, but also through banks via the digital economy. Now moving to

**[00:45:45.160] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000613)  
the external sector, we see that the external sector continue to provide some

**[00:45:50.560] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000614)  
protection from the effects of volatile external environment.

**[00:45:55.220] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000615)  
you

**[00:45:55.380] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000616)  
you

**[00:45:55.420] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000617)  
Our balance of payments, this is the total transactions of the Philippines

**[00:46:00.920] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000618)  
with the rest of the world, is in a deficit.

**[00:46:04.780] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000619)  
And an important component of that total balance of payments

**[00:46:08.860] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000620)  
is what we call the current account.

**[00:46:10.960] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000621)  
The current account captures the trade in goods as well as the trade in services.

**[00:46:18.280] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000622)  
That is also in deficit, but it has narrowed last year.

**[00:46:22.740] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000623)  
Now, for this year and 2027, next year,

**[00:46:26.600] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000624)  
the current account deficit is projected to slightly widen.

**[00:46:31.260] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000625)  
And this is something that we are monitoring.

**[00:46:34.340] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000626)  
But at the same time, we have observed that emerging markets

**[00:46:37.280] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000627)  
that continue to push for investment-led growth

**[00:46:40.260] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000628)  
usually experience such a deficit in their current account.

**[00:46:45.080] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000629)  
Now, how is this deficit being supported right now?

**[00:46:48.760] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000630)  
And here we point to very important structural flows,

**[00:46:51.980] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000631)  
the OFW remittances, the receipts from our BPO industry,

**[00:46:58.320] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000632)  
to some extent, tourism receipts, as well as foreign direct investments.

**[00:47:04.060] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000633)  
So these important inflows are vital to make sure that our external position

**[00:47:10.740] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000634)  
remains manageable and sustainable over time.

**[00:47:15.280] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000635)  
We also highlight that we maintain some buffers regarding our external,

**[00:47:21.980] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000636)  
and this is in terms of international reserves.

**[00:47:26.740] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000637)  
We show in the slide, Mr. Chair,

**[00:47:29.400] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000638)  
the recent number for our international reserves

**[00:47:32.960] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000639)  
is about $103 billion as of last month.

**[00:47:37.700] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000640)  
And is that adequate?

**[00:47:39.660] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000641)  
The answer is yes.

**[00:47:41.360] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000642)  
If you compare it, it can pay 6.7 months' worth of imports of goods and services.

**[00:47:48.320] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000643)  
It is also equivalent to 3.7.

**[00:47:51.980] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000644)  
7 times our short-term obligations,

**[00:47:57.100] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000645)  
our obligations for the next 12 months.

**[00:48:01.680] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000646)  
So overall, that is the general macroeconomic landscape

**[00:48:05.080] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000647)  
that we are working with at this time.

**[00:48:08.180] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000648)  
The key assumptions behind the proposed national budget

**[00:48:11.620] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000649)  
for fiscal year 2027 are shown, Mr. Chair, in this slide.

**[00:48:16.020] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000650)  
In terms of inflation, our forecast points to still elevated inflation,

**[00:48:21.980] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000651)  
in 2026, before easing in 2027,

**[00:48:27.040] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000652)  
but still above the inflation target of 3%.

**[00:48:30.380] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000653)  
In terms of oil prices, in recent months,

**[00:48:35.040] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000654)  
they continue to remain volatile and uncertain.

**[00:48:38.540] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000655)  
And we think that moving forward,

**[00:48:40.620] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000656)  
oil prices will reflect geopolitical developments,

**[00:48:44.580] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000657)  
including those happening in the Middle East.

**[00:48:47.800] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000658)  
In terms of exchange rate, they will be capturing,

**[00:48:50.900] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000659)  
in the near future,

**[00:48:51.680] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000660)  
different external developments,

**[00:48:54.140] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000661)  
but at the same time also reflecting possible domestic headwinds

**[00:48:59.340] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000662)  
or some improvements in domestic performance.

**[00:49:02.520] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000663)  
On domestic interest rates,

**[00:49:05.040] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000664)  
this will be reflecting the country's fiscal balance,

**[00:49:10.140] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000665)  
as well as the policy of continued consolidation

**[00:49:14.200] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000666)  
in our fiscal finances.

**[00:49:16.920] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000667)  
In terms of the international interest rates,

**[00:49:19.980] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000668)  
it will capture the expectations,

**[00:49:21.680] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000669)  
that the U.S. Fed may maintain a relatively cautious policy stance moving forward

**[00:49:28.280] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000670)  
for the rest of the year and into the next year.

**[00:49:31.340] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000671)  
Finally, our exports of goods will grow, but at a modest rate.

**[00:49:36.940] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000672)  
It will be supported by firm global demand,

**[00:49:39.980] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000673)  
particularly for electronics and manufacturers.

**[00:49:43.480] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000674)  
But there could be some challenges,

**[00:49:45.380] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000675)  
especially in the increased global trade uncertainty.

**[00:49:50.040] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000676)  
Now, let me end, Mr. Chair, with some questions.

**[00:49:51.180] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000677)  
First, in terms of inflation outlook,

**[00:49:56.180] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000678)  
we think that inflation could remain elevated over the near term,

**[00:50:00.680] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000679)  
and this will require measured action to anchor inflation expectations

**[00:50:05.880] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000680)  
and containing broadening price pressures.

**[00:50:09.280] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000681)  
We have adequate external buffers.

**[00:50:12.880] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000682)  
We also have a resilient banking system,

**[00:50:15.880] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000683)  
and these factors will be important in supporting domestic economy.

**[00:50:21.180] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000684)  
Moving forward, the BSP is prepared to take further monetary policy actions,

**[00:50:27.680] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000685)  
if needed, to help achieve price stability,

**[00:50:30.880] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000686)  
our main mandate of the BSP.

**[00:50:33.680] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000687)  
Price stability is our main contribution to promoting sustainable and durable growth.

**[00:50:41.180] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000688)  
I end here, Mr. Chair.

**[00:50:43.180] BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja** (asr-000689)  
Thank you.

**[00:51:37.960] Senator Erwin Tulfo** (asr-000713)

**[00:51:47.020] Senator Erwin Tulfo** (asr-000715)

**[00:52:02.060] Senator Erwin Tulfo** (asr-000717)

**[00:52:09.680] Senator Erwin Tulfo** (asr-000718)

**[00:52:12.960] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000720)  
That's a good question.

**[00:52:18.400] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000721)  
We've been taught.

**[00:52:19.740] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000722)  
That's a good question.

**[00:52:21.120] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000723)  
It's true that when the goods are imported, when the peso goes down, the price of those

**[00:52:29.620] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000724)  
imports will go up.

**[00:52:32.940] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000725)

**[00:52:42.460] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000726)  
of the exchange rate on inflation will be higher.

**[00:52:46.280] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000727)  
Pero kung mabagal ang galaw, hindi masyadong tinatamaan yung inflation.

**[00:52:49.740] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000728)

**[00:52:59.380] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000729)

**[00:53:06.880] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000730)

**[00:53:15.660] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000731)  
Masyadong mahal ang exports natin.

**[00:53:19.740] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000732)  
Kulang na kulang ang exports natin.

**[00:53:21.740] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000733)

**[00:53:26.080] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000734)  
Pwedeng pigilin para bumagal pero hindi kayang pigilin, hindi kayang i-fix, hindi kayang 60 pesos. Ganun lang.

**[00:53:34.280] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000735)  
Hindi kaya yun eh.

**[00:53:35.340] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000736)  
Maubusan tayong reserves.

**[00:53:37.460] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000737)  
Maubusan tayong dollars.

**[00:53:39.780] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000738)  
Pero kung mabagal, hindi naman masyadong inflationary.

**[00:53:42.780] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000739)  
But hopefully, our exports will grow.

**[00:53:46.420] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000740)  
Our exports are too low.

**[00:53:48.220] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000741)  
Our exports.

**[00:53:49.320] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000742)  
That's the...

**[00:53:49.740] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000743)  
That's our challenge here in the exchange rate.

**[00:53:56.720] Senator Erwin Tulfo** (asr-000744)  
I just have one follow-up question on that.

**[00:53:59.660] Senator Erwin Tulfo** (asr-000745)  
So, what are you studying?

**[00:54:02.760] Senator Erwin Tulfo** (asr-000746)  
How do we go around this?

**[00:54:04.540] Senator Erwin Tulfo** (asr-000747)  
How can we improve this?

**[00:54:06.560] Senator Erwin Tulfo** (asr-000748)  
If we can't do anything about the exchange rate, because we depend so much right now

**[00:54:14.100] Senator Erwin Tulfo** (asr-000749)  
on the remittances of our OFWs, and we thank God that they are there.

**[00:54:19.400] Senator Erwin Tulfo** (asr-000750)  
Otherwise, wala na talaga.

**[00:54:19.740] Senator Erwin Tulfo** (asr-000751)  
Bagsak na itong ekonomiya natin.

**[00:54:22.880] Senator Erwin Tulfo** (asr-000752)  
So, other than remittances, sabi niyo, hindi rin po puwede yung exports dahil napakabagal.

**[00:54:29.040] Senator Erwin Tulfo** (asr-000753)  
Isa sa mga sakit ng ulo ng Bureau of Customs right now, ang daming pumapasok po na container imports.

**[00:54:35.980] Senator Erwin Tulfo** (asr-000754)  
Pero pag-export, natatambak ngayon diyan sa pier, sa mga kung saan-saan, masakit na po ang ulo ng commissioner natin.

**[00:54:42.800] Senator Erwin Tulfo** (asr-000755)  
how to dispose those empty containers.

**[00:54:46.180] Senator Erwin Tulfo** (asr-000756)  
So, anong nakikita ninyo in your studies?

**[00:54:49.260] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000757)  
Now, we can do something about it.

**[00:54:51.100] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000758)  
Gumawa tayong paraan na palakasin ang exports.

**[00:54:59.800] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000759)  
So, for example, Pax Silica, it could help with exports.

**[00:55:05.080] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000760)  
And Luzon Economic Corridor, it could help with exports.

**[00:55:10.480] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000761)  
But it may take some time before we can do it.

**[00:55:18.140] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000762)  
Ang isa pang consideration dyan, Senator, yung savings rate natin.

**[00:55:25.600] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000766)  
Kasi pag binilang mo yung remittances at saka yung BPO, ang diperensya ng pumapasok na pera at saka lumalabas, ang tawag dun current account.

**[00:55:37.240] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000767)  
Negative din

**[00:55:39.660] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000768)  
ang current account natin, matagal nang negative.

**[00:55:44.200] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000769)  
As much as possible, I hope our savings will increase.

**[00:55:47.500] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000770)  
That's the long-term solution.

**[00:55:50.140] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000771)  
It's a bit difficult to say this, Senator.

**[00:55:53.720] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000772)  
But it's a bold decision.

**[00:55:54.400] Senator Erwin Tulfo** (asr-000773)  
I agree with you, sir.

**[00:56:01.880] Senator Erwin Tulfo** (asr-000774)  
Because we spend so much higher than what we make.

**[00:56:06.060] Senator Erwin Tulfo** (asr-000775)  
You know, you only spend how much you make.

**[00:56:12.420] Senator Erwin Tulfo** (asr-000776)  
But we spend more than what we make.

**[00:56:15.900] Senator Erwin Tulfo** (asr-000777)  
It's like a family.

**[00:56:17.240] Senator Erwin Tulfo** (asr-000778)  
The father and the mother have a salary of 50,000.

**[00:56:20.920] Senator Erwin Tulfo** (asr-000779)  
The expenses are 80,000.

**[00:56:23.120] Senator Erwin Tulfo** (asr-000780)  
How can you save?

**[00:56:24.400] Senator Erwin Tulfo** (asr-000781)  
That's the problem.

**[00:56:25.400] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000782)  
That's the debt.

**[00:56:26.700] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000783)  
And for the country as a whole, to finance it, it's a bigger investment than savings.

**[00:56:32.180] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000784)  
So to finance it, we'll borrow from abroad.

**[00:56:36.900] Senator Erwin Tulfo** (asr-000785)  
Thank you.

**[00:56:37.620] Senator Erwin Tulfo** (asr-000786)  
That's all for me, Mr. Chair.

**[00:56:39.460] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-000787)

Thank you, Mr. Chairman.

**[00:56:42.700] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-000789)  
Magandang umaga po, Governor Remolona.

**[00:56:45.760] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-000790)  
Last time we met, last year, di ba?

**[00:56:49.040] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000791)  
Yes.

**[00:56:49.760] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-000792)  
So once a year lang tayo nakikita, samantalahin ko na lang tanungin.

**[00:56:52.500] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000793)  
Go ahead.

**[00:56:52.640] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-000794)  
Tama po ba yung aking understanding na ang easing ng inflation ay nakabasis sa assumption na bumaba ba yung prices ng oil at saka sundan ko yung kay Senator Tulfo, yung stable yung exchange rate natin.

**[00:57:11.400] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-000795)  
Tama po ba yun?

**[00:57:12.840] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000796)  
Tama po yun.

**[00:57:13.620] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-000797)  
So ang tanong ko po, dahil nagbukas yung, kasi nakita ko yung graph ng inflation sa presentation,

**[00:57:22.640] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-000798)  
Nagbukas po yung Strait of Hormus June this year.

**[00:57:33.240] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-000799)  
Kasi nga nagkaroon ng memorandum of understanding between the US and Iran na buksan. Pero temporary lang dahil August, hindi naman fully open, hindi naman fully closed pero nagsara uli.

**[00:57:41.900] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-000800)  
So ang tanong ko po, paano natin matatarget yung inflation, yung movement kung beyond the government control,

**[00:57:52.640] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-000801)  
Yung mga factors o yung drivers like yung oil prices, exchange rate, ano po yung ating gagawing measures kasi hindi natin abot yun eh. Wala tayong kontrol eh.

**[00:58:04.440] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-000802)  
So, at our end, ano po yung pwede lang natin gawin para masustain natin yung inflation rate?

**[00:58:10.700] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000803)  
Tama po kayo, Sen.

**[00:58:12.700] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000804)  
Talagang wala tayong magagawa sa price of oil.

**[00:58:15.840] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000805)  
Global yan.

**[00:58:16.800] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000806)  
At saka yung share natin sa demand for oil, 4% lang.

**[00:58:22.640] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000807)  
So, kahit anong gawin natin, hindi natin mababago yun.

**[00:58:26.740] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000808)  
Yung price of oil, tinatamaan naman yung fertilizer.

**[00:58:29.600] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000809)  
Dahil yung fertilizer natin galing din sa oil.

**[00:58:32.180] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000810)  
So tatamaan yung presyo ng pagkain, presyo ng bigas.

**[00:58:37.800] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000811)  
So ang tinitira namin yung second round effects.

**[00:58:41.940] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000812)  
Kasi yung second round effects kaya nating—

**[00:58:44.140] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000813)  
Demand side yung second round effects.

**[00:58:46.120] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000814)  
So may magagawa tayo.

**[00:58:47.840] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000815)  
Kaya lang mabagal.

**[00:58:49.060] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-000816)  
Like what po?

**[00:58:51.020] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000818)  
Yung ibang mga services.

**[00:58:52.640] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000819)  
Halimbawa, yung presyo ng services, restaurants, yung mga ganoon.

**[00:58:58.860] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000820)  
Kaya nating pahinayin yung inflation doon.

**[00:59:03.020] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000821)  
Pero over time, mapapababa naman natin.

**[00:59:07.260] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000822)  
Matagal lang.

**[00:59:09.580] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-000822-split-2)  
For my education lang po, can we be more specific kung ano yung mga measures?

**[00:59:11.900] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000823)  
So, ang strategy namin dahil ang number one tool na namin, yung interest rate.

**[00:59:22.640] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000824)  
So, pag tumaas ang interest rate, mapapababa natin yung demand ng mga services,

**[00:59:30.320] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000825)  
o yung mga tinatawag natin na second round effects ng mga items.

**[00:59:38.320] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000826)  
So yun na muna.

**[00:59:39.860] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-000827)  
How much po ang influence nung ating kayang gawin?

**[00:59:43.880] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000828)  
Inaabot tayo ng two years bago natin mabalik sa 3%.

**[00:59:47.900] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-000829)  
Anyway, thank you, Mr. Chairman.

**[00:59:50.680] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-000830)  
Thank you, Governor.

**[00:59:51.480] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000831)

**[00:59:52.640] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-000832)  
Thank you, Senator Lacson, Senator Hontiveros.

**[00:59:56.020] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-000833)  
Salamat, Mr. Chair.

**[00:59:57.760] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-000834)  
At magandang umaga po muli, Gov.

**[01:00:00.110] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-000835)  
Hindi lang naman po yung Pilipinas pero yung buong mundo ay naapektohan ng mga global headwinds. Pero bakit ang taas ng inflation figures natin kumpara sa mga kapitbahay natin, sa atin 6.2%, samantala ang Vietnam 4.4%, ang Thailand 1.95% at ang Malaysia 1.8%.

**[01:00:25.490] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-000836)  
So ano po yung nag-a-account para sa diferensyang iyon na ang samanong epekto po sa atin?

**[01:00:36.640] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000837)  
Tayo yung napuruhan ng oil prices eh. Yung gaya ng Indonesia, merong oil sila although nag-iimport pa rin pero meron silang oil.

**[01:00:44.800] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000838)  
Malaysia, ganun din, may oil sila pero nag-iimport sila ng konti. So tayo, wala tayong oil talaga eh. So malakas ang tama talaga sa atin.

**[01:00:53.680] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000839)  
Tapos, just to oversimplify, Senator, pwede mong hatiin yung mga economists,

**[01:00:58.960] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000840)  
Yung may oil at saka yung walang oil. Wala tayong oil. Pwede nyo rin hatiin yung mga economists. Yung may AI at saka walang AI.

**[01:01:08.300] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000841)  
Tayo, wala tayong AI eh. Na totoong AI. So yung merong AI na mga economists, nakakompensate yung kanilang AI sector sa pagkakulangan ng oil.

**[01:01:22.960] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000842)  
So tayo, talo talaga tayo dun sa ganun mga aspects.

**[01:01:27.440] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000843)  
Although this is two oversimplified things.

**[01:01:31.000] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-000844)  
Kahit sabi nyo po gov oversimplification, so dalawang factors, the haves and the have-nots, langis at saka AI, could you possibly give a third para may indication din po kami,

**[01:01:43.140] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-000845)  
kahit sa pag-examine ng anong dapat na budget para sa 2027 na adjustan po namin para masuportahan din yung mga measures na ginagawa nyo sa Banko Sentral

**[01:01:55.080] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-000846)  
na i-tame at i-control ang inflation at ibalik siya.

**[01:01:58.960] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-000847)  
So talaga dun sa trajectory papunta sa inflation target kahit by year 2028 pa.

**[01:02:06.480] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000848)  
Kung meron man sir.

**[01:02:09.280] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000849)  
Walang masyadong obvious eh pero.

**[01:02:20.000] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-000850)  
So itong dalawa po ang dalawang pinaka-obvious na may posibleng positive effect sa pag-tame ng inflation.

**[01:02:23.590] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000850-split-2)  
Dalawang pinaka-obvious po.

**[01:02:32.200] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-000851)  
Alright, well noted po.

**[01:02:33.980] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-000852)  
Salamat po, Governor. Salamat po, Mr. Chair.

**[01:02:36.080] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-000853)  
Thank you, Senator Ontiberos. Next is Senator Pangilinan.

**[01:02:40.420] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000854)  
Thank you, Magandang Maga, Governor, Deputy Governor.

**[01:02:45.000] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000855)  
Si Deputy Governor Abinoha and I sat in the NFA Council when I was Chairman and you were representing the BSP.

**[01:02:55.000] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000856)  
Food inflation actually is a driver of nationwide inflation.

**[01:03:00.980] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000857)  
In fact, to be specific, rice inflation.

**[01:03:03.980] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000858)  
Rice inflation is a big driver, either driving it up or driving it down.

**[01:03:11.020] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000859)  
Would you consider that, Governor, one of the interventions that needs immediate addressing so that we can bring down nationwide inflation?

**[01:03:22.160] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000860)  
I say this because, and I think Deputy Governor Abinoha will remember or perhaps you will recall,

**[01:03:31.040] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000861)  
during our watch with the NFA having the...

**[01:03:33.980] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000862)

**[01:03:36.180] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000863)

**[01:03:50.900] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000864)

**[01:03:57.320] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000865)  
So much so that within one year,

**[01:04:01.500] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000866)  
rice inflation dropped from 15%.

**[01:04:03.980] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000867)

**[01:04:05.980] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000868)

**[01:04:08.860] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000869)  
And by September of 2015,

**[01:04:13.160] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000870)  
we registered the lowest inflation

**[01:04:15.340] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000871)  
in 20 years

**[01:04:17.640] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000872)  
from 1995 to 2015.

**[01:04:22.300] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000873)  
You will recall that,

**[01:04:24.060] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000874)  
DepGov Abinoha.

**[01:04:26.700] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000875)  
So,

**[01:04:28.060] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000876)  
should not that be one major consideration for our

**[01:04:31.460] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000877)  
Executive Department?

**[01:04:33.980] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000878)  
How do we manage, bring down, food inflation, particularly rice inflation?

**[01:04:38.860] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000879)  
Tama kayo, Senator.

**[01:04:43.230] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000880)  
Food is 37% of our index.

**[01:04:48.030] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000881)  
So, malaking share ng index.

**[01:04:51.030] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000882)  
For the lower 30% of our household, food is 50% of their basket.

**[01:04:59.030] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000883)  
Now, rice is very special.

**[01:05:02.030] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000884)  
Ang rice kasi, ang tawag namin din, salient price.

**[01:05:05.230] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000885)  
Napapansin

**[01:05:06.150] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000886)  
ng mga tao, yung presyo ng bigas,

**[01:05:08.150] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000887)  
na-affect yung expectations nila.

**[01:05:11.150] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000888)  
Pag tumaas yung presyo ng bigas, may effects sa expectations.

**[01:05:14.150] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000889)  
Yung expectations, ano yan eh, part of the mechanism for inflation.

**[01:05:20.150] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000890)  
So, maganda kung hindi tumaas masyado yung presyo ng bigas.

**[01:05:26.150] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000891)  
Ang makakabuti, hindi po yung lalagyan natin ng cap, hindi masyado nakakatulong yung cap.

**[01:05:35.150] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000892)  
Ang mas mabuti, hindi po yung lalagyan natin ng cap, hindi masyado nakakatulong yung cap.

**[01:05:36.150] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000893)  
Ang mas mabuti, mataas natin, itaas natin yung productivity ng ating agriculture para mas malaki ang production natin ng rice.

**[01:05:45.150] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000894)  
Unfortunately, in terms of agri-exports, we continue to be a net importer instead of a net exporter.

**[01:05:57.460] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000895)  
And we're doing very, not naman negligible, but nakakalungkot kung inkumpara yung ating agri-export.

**[01:06:07.460] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000896)  
We're doing agri-exports sa Thailand, Indonesia.

**[01:06:11.460] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000897)  
They're doing almost 60 plus billion dollars worth of agri-exports while we're doing about nine.

**[01:06:18.460] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000898)  
So clearly, something is not right with precisely why food inflation,

**[01:06:26.460] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000899)  
why nationwide inflation is high because food inflation is high.

**[01:06:30.460] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000900)  
Food inflation is high because productivity is low, supply is low.

**[01:06:36.460] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000901)  
And therefore, when demand is high and supply is low, then prices will obviously go up.

**[01:06:44.460] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000902)  
So it's actually a very basic, simple problem.

**[01:06:52.460] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000903)  
I mean, simply defined, articulated problem.

**[01:06:56.460] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000904)  
Now, the challenge is how do you bring down food prices?

**[01:06:59.460] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000905)  
How do you increase productivity?

**[01:07:01.460] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000906)  
I mean, that's really now up to the executive department through the DA.

**[01:07:05.460] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000907)  
And the DepDev

**[01:07:07.460] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000908)  
But you will agree that if we address food inflation by providing the right supply,

**[01:07:21.460] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000909)  
we will bring down nationwide inflation.

**[01:07:24.460] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000910)  
Absolutely. Absolutely, Senator.

**[01:07:26.460] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000911)

**[01:07:28.460] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-000912)  
Thank you, Senator Pangilinan.

**[01:08:03.460] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000919)

**[01:08:47.800] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000932)

**[01:09:00.800] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000934)

**[01:09:03.800] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000935)

**[01:09:05.800] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000936)

**[01:09:10.800] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000937)

**[01:09:13.800] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000938)

**[01:09:15.800] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000939)

**[01:09:42.800] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000946)

**[01:09:46.800] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000947)

**[01:09:50.800] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000948)

**[01:09:53.800] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000949)  
What we've done on our side, which is what we can do,

**[01:10:00.490] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000950)

**[01:10:03.490] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000951)

**[01:10:09.490] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000953)  
If this happens, what is inflation?

**[01:10:12.490] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000954)

**[01:10:16.490] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000955)

**[01:10:21.490] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000956)

**[01:10:32.490] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000958)  
In Iran, Governor Eli.

**[01:10:35.490] BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.** (asr-000959)

**[01:10:38.490] Senator Francis Kiko Pangilinan** (asr-000960)

**[01:10:40.490] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-000961)

Senator Pangilinan.

**[01:56:12.250] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002600)

**[01:56:15.350] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002601)  
Foremost among

**[01:56:16.570] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002603)

**[01:56:18.610] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002604)

**[01:56:19.090] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002605)

**[01:56:20.990] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002608)

**[01:56:22.530] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002609)

**[01:56:23.290] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002610)  
as a lower

**[01:56:24.290] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002611)

**[01:56:24.870] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002612)  
country or

The country's

**[01:56:27.380] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002615)  
GNI per

**[01:56:28.380] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002616)

**[01:56:29.380] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002617)

**[01:56:30.380] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002618)

**[01:56:31.380] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002619)

**[01:56:33.380] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002621)

**[01:56:34.380] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002622)
