**[01:56:35.380] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002623)  
threshold of

**[01:56:36.380] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002624)  
4,636

**[01:56:37.380] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002625)  
US dollars.

**[01:56:39.260] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002628)  
the Philippines has also moved closer to its ASEAN peers through significant income gains.

**[01:56:51.540] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002641)  
Although significant income gains remain, reaching upper middle income status is an important achievement.

**[01:57:00.140] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002653)  
But it's not the end in itself.

**[01:57:03.800] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002657)  
The greater challenge is to translate progress into better jobs, higher incomes, and improve living standards for Filipinos.

**[01:57:14.060] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002665)  
To do so, we must first understand the factors behind the recent loss of economic momentum.

**[01:57:23.170] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002670)  
This slowdown largely reflected weaker domestic demand, as governance and corruption concerns,

**[01:57:31.370] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002674)  
and the Middle East conflict weighed on consumer and business confidence.

**[01:57:37.830] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002679)  
Domestic demand grew by only 1.5% in the first half of 2026,

**[01:57:42.470] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002684)  
down from 5.7% in the same period the previous year.

**[01:57:49.920] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002692)  
Investment contracted 6.5%, driven by a sharp decline in public construction.

**[01:57:58.240] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002700)  
Household consumption growth also eased to 2.9% amid elevated inflation and weaker confidence

**[01:58:08.590] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002710)  
Exports provided some support, growing by 10%

**[01:58:12.650] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002716)  
On the production side, however, services remained the principal source of growth

**[01:58:19.190] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002723)  
while industry, contracted, and agriculture made only a modest contribution

**[01:58:27.300] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002727)  
The slowdown in economic activity has also begun to affect the labor market.

**[01:58:34.680] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002735)  
The post-pandemic expansion created 4 million net jobs between the first half of 2022 and the first half of 2026,

**[01:58:45.820] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002746)  
demonstrating how economic growth can create opportunities and improve livelihoods.

**[01:58:53.500] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002752)  
However, as growth slowed, total employment declined by 166,000 over the past year.

**[01:59:03.600] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002765)  
The unemployment rate also rose to 4.2% in June 2026, up from 3.1% a year earlier.

**[01:59:14.640] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002774)  
These recent developments underscore the urgency of restoring economic momentum and generating more and better quality jobs.

**[01:59:25.750] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002781)  
Nonetheless, even with the recent slowdown, the longer-run benefits of

**[01:59:31.280] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002782)  
economic growth extended beyond employment to include poverty reduction. Poverty declined substantially, regardless of the poverty

**[01:59:42.020] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002783)  
threshold or norm applied. As income growth outpaced inflation, and gains were broadly shared

**[01:59:49.760] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002784)  
across all income deciles.

**[01:59:54.140] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002812)  
Based on the country's official poverty lines and preliminary estimates for 2025,

**[02:00:00.680] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002813)  
or not preliminary estimates, they are already official estimates,

**[02:00:04.520] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002834)  
poverty incidence among Filipinos fell from 15.5% in 2023 to 9.7% in 2025.

**[02:00:15.900] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002838)  
This means that 6.5 million Filipinos were lifted out of poverty over this period.

**[02:00:23.070] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002840)  
This reflects the recovery of incomes and employment

**[02:00:28.050] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002841)  
as well as sustained implementation of social protection programs.

**[02:00:33.810] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002843)  
However, these hard-earned gains remain vulnerable,

**[02:00:39.990] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002844)  
especially to high inflation.

**[02:00:44.840] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002845)  
As Governor Remolona discussed earlier,

**[02:00:47.880] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002846)  
inflation surged beginning in March,

**[02:00:51.620] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002847)  
largely driven by the impact of the Middle East conflict

**[02:00:54.520] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002848)  
on global oil and commodity prices.

**[02:00:58.700] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002849)  
Headline inflation

**[02:00:59.880] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002850)  
is slightly to 6.2% in July,

**[02:01:03.420] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002851)  
down from 6.4% in June,

**[02:01:06.980] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002852)  
but it remains well above the government's target range.

**[02:01:11.800] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002853)  
High inflation erodes household purchasing power,

**[02:01:15.920] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002854)  
disproportionately affecting the poor

**[02:01:18.500] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002855)  
and low-income families.

**[02:01:21.660] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002856)  
The burden is even heavier when food prices rise faster

**[02:01:25.820] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002857)  
than non-food prices, because food accounts for a much larger share

**[02:01:30.650] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002860)  
of total consumption spending

**[02:01:32.450] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002861)  
among low-income families than among high-income families.

**[02:01:38.980] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002864)  
If inflation remains elevated,

**[02:01:41.560] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002865)  
it could slow or even reverse our recent advances

**[02:01:46.000] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002866)  
in poverty reduction.

**[02:01:48.000] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002867)  
Protecting our progress goes beyond addressing

**[02:01:54.160] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002868)  
the immediate concerns of slower growth

**[02:01:57.040] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002869)  
and elevated inflation.

**[02:01:58.780] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002870)  
Protecting our progress goes beyond addressing the immediate concerns

**[02:01:59.860] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002871)  
of slower growth and elevated inflation.

**[02:02:00.360] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002872)  
It also requires tackling persistent

**[02:02:01.340] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002873)  
structural constraints that continue to

**[02:02:02.060] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002874)  
constraints that continue to limit the economy's productive capacity and resilience.

**[02:02:08.440] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002875)  
Let me now turn to these constraints, Mr. Chair.

**[02:02:13.200] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002876)  
A central structural challenge is the economy's heavy reliance on household consumption on

**[02:02:20.540] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002877)  
the demand side and on the services side of our economy and the production side.

**[02:02:26.280] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002878)  
Consumption remains the primary driver of economic growth, while contributions of fixed

**[02:02:33.060] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002879)  
investment and net exports have been modest.

**[02:02:38.280] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002880)  
Similarly, services account for most of the expansion, while agriculture and industry

**[02:02:44.700] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002881)  
have contributed much less.

**[02:02:48.900] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002882)  
This experience of successful economies shows that sustained progress requires mobilizing

**[02:02:56.080] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002883)  
other sources of growth.

**[02:02:58.240] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002884)  
We must therefore broaden our growth pillars by strengthening investments and exports while

**[02:03:05.640] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002885)  
revitalizing agriculture and industry.

**[02:03:08.980] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002886)  
The urgency of this task is evident from our performance relative to our ASEAN peers.

**[02:03:19.190] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002887)  
As the chart shows, Philippines continues to trail several neighboring economies in

**[02:03:26.370] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002888)  
both fixed investments and exports.

**[02:03:29.650] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002889)  
Despite improvement in recent years, investment expands productive capacity, facilitates the

**[02:03:38.020] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002890)  
adoption of new technologies, and creates better jobs.

**[02:03:42.780] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002891)  
Exports enable domestic firms to access larger markets, achieve economies of scale, and become

**[02:03:49.540] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002892)  
more competitive.

**[02:03:52.890] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002893)  
Mobilizing greater investments and improving export competitiveness will depend critically

**[02:03:57.970] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002894)  
on high-quality and reliable infrastructure.

**[02:04:05.270] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002896)  
The Government has substantially increased productive infrastructure spending in recent

**[02:04:11.130] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002897)  
years, yet this higher level of expenditure has not fully translated into stronger infrastructure

**[02:04:18.870] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002898)  
competitiveness.

**[02:04:20.310] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002899)  
This gap shows that the level of spending alone is not enough.

**[02:04:25.930] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002900)  
We must also improve project selection, appraisal, procurement, implementation,

**[02:04:32.390] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002901)  
and maintenance

**[02:04:33.370] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002902)  
to ensure

**[02:04:34.230] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002903)  
that public resources deliver high-quality infrastructure

**[02:04:38.930] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002904)  
on time and at reasonable cost.

**[02:04:44.140] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002905)  
Closing our infrastructure gaps will reduce production and logistics costs,

**[02:04:48.560] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002906)  
connect people and markets, attract private investment,

**[02:04:52.580] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002907)  
and strengthen the country's competitiveness.

**[02:04:57.290] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002908)  
Beyond physical infrastructure,

**[02:05:00.190] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002909)  
faster growth also requires greater innovation and stronger productivity.

**[02:05:04.610] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002910)  
The Philippines, Mr. Chair, has made encouraging progress in innovation

**[02:05:11.170] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002911)  
as reflected in its improved ranking in the Global Innovation Index.

**[02:05:17.750] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002912)  
However, this has yet to translate into stronger overall productivity,

**[02:05:24.150] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002913)  
the efficiency with which the economy uses its resources to produce goods and services.

**[02:05:29.810] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002914)  
As the chart on the right shows,

**[02:05:34.030] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002915)  
our productivity,

**[02:05:34.610] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002916)  
performance remains weak relative to several of our regional peers.

**[02:05:42.960] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002917)  
Innovation contributes to development only when new knowledge and technologies

**[02:05:47.860] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002918)  
are widely adopted by firms, farms, and workers,

**[02:05:52.800] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002919)  
and when they are translated into more efficient production,

**[02:05:57.680] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002920)  
better products, and higher value activities.

**[02:06:01.360] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002921)  
We must therefore strengthen the connection among research,

**[02:06:04.900] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002922)  
skills development,

**[02:06:06.240] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002923)  
technology adoption,

**[02:06:08.240] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002924)  
commercialization,

**[02:06:10.240] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002925)  
and production.

**[02:06:12.240] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002926)  
The weaknesses we have discussed do not stem from a single source.

**[02:06:16.240] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002927)  
They reflect persistent and interconnected constraints across markets and institutions

**[02:06:22.760] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002928)  
that continue to hinder investment, productivity, and diversification.

**[02:06:29.760] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002929)  
Addressing them requires coordinated action by government,

**[02:06:36.240] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002930)  
in close coordination with Congress, the private sector, and other stakeholders.

**[02:06:42.840] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002931)  
This brings us to our growth targets and priorities for advancing the economy.

**[02:06:47.680] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002932)  
Our direction remains anchored in the Philippine Development Plan.

**[02:06:54.900] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002933)  
Over the Administration's final two years, the focus is on accelerating execution,

**[02:07:01.540] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002934)  
resolving implementation bottlenecks, and translating reforms into concrete results.

**[02:07:08.900] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002936)  
Given the slowdown in recent quarters, economic growth is projected to be at 3.5% to 4.5% in 2026.

**[02:07:20.760] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002937)  
With faster implementation of public programs and infrastructure projects, improved domestic supply conditions, and restored consumer and investor confidence, growth is expected to recover to 5% to 6% over the next two years.

**[02:07:37.460] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002938)  
Inflation is expected to remain elevated in 2026, as already shown earlier by the BSP.

**[02:07:46.780] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002939)  
Ease to 4% to 5% in 2027, and return to the government's 2% to 4% target range by 2028.

**[02:08:00.270] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002940)  
Meanwhile, employment conditions are expected to improve as the economy recovers, keeping unemployment within the government's target range.

**[02:08:11.470] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002941)  
These targets are attainable, but they remain subject to significant domestic and external risks.

**[02:08:18.770] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002942)  
Foremost among the domestic risks are further delays in the execution of public investments, leading to continued underspending, as well as continuing governance concerns that could further weaken consumer and investor confidence.

**[02:08:40.530] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002944)  
Severe weather disturbances could also constrain food production, and intensify inflationary pressure.

**[02:08:47.040] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002945)  
Externally, the prolonged Middle East conflict could keep global oil and commodity prices elevated, while geopolitical and trade tensions may weaken global demand and disrupt supply chains.

**[02:09:02.780] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002946)  
To manage this risk, we have established clear imperatives.

**[02:09:08.900] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002947)  
In the near term,

**[02:09:10.980] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002949)  
our priorities are to

**[02:09:11.980] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002950)  
protect vulnerable households, accelerate public investments, and restore confidence.

**[02:09:19.260] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002951)  
First, we will protect poor and low-income families against high food prices

**[02:09:24.300] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002952)  
and supply disruptions through targeted and timely assistance,

**[02:09:29.240] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002953)  
while strengthening the domestic food supply and maintaining adequate buffers.

**[02:09:36.100] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002954)  
Second, implementing agencies will accelerate high-impact infrastructure projects

**[02:09:41.520] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002955)  
through catch-up plans with clear milestones and accountability measures.

**[02:09:46.380] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002956)  
This is essential to reverse underspending and restore public investment as a driver of growth.

**[02:09:54.780] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002957)  
Third, we need to address governance and corruption concerns

**[02:09:59.820] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002958)  
by strengthening transparency and accountability,

**[02:10:04.180] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002959)  
improving monitoring, and ensuring the efficient use of public resources.

**[02:10:10.620] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002960)  
In the short-to-medium term,

**[02:10:12.840] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002961)  
limited public resources must be directed toward high-impact, implementation-ready investments.

**[02:10:21.220] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002962)  
Priorities include addressing learning poverty and classroom shortages,

**[02:10:26.860] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002963)  
equipping workers with future-ready skills,

**[02:10:30.280] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002964)  
strengthening primary health care, particularly in underserved areas,

**[02:10:35.160] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002965)  
raising farm productivity through climate-resilient technologies and post-harvest infrastructure,

**[02:10:42.840] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002966)  
and accelerating transport, logistics, energy, and digital infrastructure

**[02:10:49.540] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002967)  
through the Build Better, More program and public-private partnerships.

**[02:10:55.340] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002968)  
These investments must be pursued while safeguarding fiscal sustainability.

**[02:11:02.240] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002969)  
This requires stronger coordination across planning, investment programming, budgeting,

**[02:11:09.000] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002970)  
and execution of infrastructure and social programs.

**[02:11:12.840] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002971)  
We also need to improve spending efficiency,

**[02:11:16.060] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002972)  
modernize tax and customs administration,

**[02:11:20.220] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002973)  
and revenue measures that do not erode the government's fiscal position.

**[02:11:27.280] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002974)  
Looking ahead, sustained structural reforms will be needed to raise productivity,

**[02:11:34.460] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002975)  
strengthen competitiveness, and expand the economy's long-term growth potential.

**[02:11:41.080] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002976)  
Key priorities include ensuring more reliable and affordable energy,

**[02:11:44.920] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002977)  
by expanding renewable generation, modernizing the power grid,

**[02:11:54.760] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002978)  
and streamlining the net metering and permitting processes,

**[02:11:59.420] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002979)  
and strengthening competition in the electricity market.

**[02:12:05.700] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002980)  
Domestic production and external competitiveness must likewise be strengthened

**[02:12:10.800] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002981)  
by moving into higher value segments of global value chains,

**[02:12:15.700] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002982)  
fostering stronger linkages between

**[02:12:17.140] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002983)  
multinational and domestic firms,

**[02:12:21.140] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002984)  
sustaining the country's advantages or advantage in services,

**[02:12:25.300] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002985)  
and expanding market access for Philippine exports.

**[02:12:29.980] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002986)  
Deeper financial and capital markets will also be essential

**[02:12:34.400] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002987)  
to mobilize long-term financing for infrastructure and productive enterprises.

**[02:12:42.380] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002988)  
Legislation will be indispensable to advance advancing this reform agenda.

**[02:12:48.280] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002989)  
The priority measures fall into four broad areas.

**[02:12:55.380] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002990)  
Governance and anti-corruption reforms include measures addressing political dynasties, the party-led system, freedom of information, bank secrecy, and public budgeting.

**[02:13:11.840] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002991)  
Economic growth and resilience measures include tax reforms and amendments affecting the coconut and fisheries sector.

**[02:13:18.340] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002992)  
Energy priorities include amendments to EPIRA and waste-to-energy legislation.

**[02:13:26.680] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002993)  
Measures in education, health, and social protection aim to improve nutrition, accelerate classroom construction, expand access to education, and strengthen assistance to vulnerable Filipinos.

**[02:13:40.960] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002994)  
Again, Congress' continued partnership will be critical to advancing these reforms.

**[02:13:47.440] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002995)  
Sustaining

**[02:13:48.280] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002996)  
growth, and improving the lives of Filipinos.

**[02:13:54.440] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002997)  
As we enter the final years of the administration, our objective is to turn reforms into results.

**[02:14:02.220] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002998)  
This means accelerating the implementation of high-impact programs and projects, the surest path to recovering growth, extending its benefits to more Filipinos, and building an economy resilient enough to withstand future shocks.

**[02:14:20.480] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-002999)  
None of this can be achieved by any agency alone.

**[02:14:24.820] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-003000)  
It requires efficient and coordinated action across the entire government.

**[02:14:28.860] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-003001)  
We look forward to our continued partnership with this committee as we work to deliver stronger, broader, and more inclusive growth in the years ahead.

**[02:14:41.100] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-003002)  
Thank you, Mr. Chairman.

**[02:23:20.410] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003261)

**[02:23:23.030] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003262)  
Our fiscal position

**[02:23:24.530] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003263)  
today has been shaped by key

**[02:23:26.470] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003264)

**[02:23:28.470] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003265)  
the circumstances this

**[02:23:30.370] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003266)  
administration inherited.

**[02:23:31.670] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003267)  
To the global conditions

**[02:23:33.710] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003268)  
that have influenced our fiscal path

**[02:23:35.830] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003269)  
since then. Allow me

**[02:23:37.970] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003270)  
to discuss this briefly to provide

**[02:23:39.810] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003271)  
context to where we are today

**[02:23:41.470] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003272)  
and where we are headed.

**[02:23:43.730] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003273)  
When the Marcos Jr. Administration

**[02:23:45.890] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003274)  
assumed office in 2022,

**[02:23:48.230] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003275)  
we started with a

**[02:23:49.510] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003276)  
12.79 trillion

**[02:23:51.650] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003277)  
debt, the bulk of which

**[02:23:53.650] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003278)  
was incurred from pandemic

**[02:23:55.850] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003279)  
spending. So when the

**[02:23:57.870] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003280)  
economy began to recover, the challenge

**[02:23:59.850] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003281)  
before the administration was clear.

**[02:24:01.670] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003282)  
Rebuild fiscal space

**[02:24:03.830] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003283)  
while continuing to support economic

**[02:24:05.850] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003284)  
recovery and investing in the

**[02:24:07.950] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003285)  
country's long-term growth.

**[02:24:10.350] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003286)  
As a response,

**[02:24:12.450] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003287)  
we crafted the country's

**[02:24:13.710] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003288)  
medium-term fiscal framework in

**[02:24:15.650] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003289)  
2022, the government's

**[02:24:17.910] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003290)  
blueprint for gradually reducing

**[02:24:19.730] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003291)  
our deficit and debt while

**[02:24:21.710] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003292)  
creating jobs, increasing

**[02:24:23.750] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003293)  
people's incomes, and reducing

**[02:24:25.870] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003294)  
poverty. It set

**[02:24:27.990] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003295)  
us on a path of gradual and

**[02:24:29.670] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003296)  
sustained fiscal consolidation,

**[02:24:31.670] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003297)  
to restore fiscal space

**[02:24:33.530] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003298)  
while continuing to invest in the

**[02:24:35.330] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003299)  
foundations of growth.

**[02:24:37.610] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003300)  
But our recovery has not

**[02:24:39.430] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003301)  
happened in an easy environment.

**[02:24:42.490] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003302)  
Over the years,

**[02:24:43.790] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003303)  
external pressures and global

**[02:24:45.310] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003304)  
uncertainties have disrupted supply

**[02:24:47.450] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003305)  
chains and pushed inflation up,

**[02:24:50.010] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003306)  
affecting the pace of growth.

**[02:24:52.430] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003307)  
In this context,

**[02:24:53.430] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003308)  
we had to recalibrate our growth

**[02:24:55.290] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003309)  
and fiscal targets to keep them realistic

**[02:24:57.530] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003310)  
and responsive to evolving

**[02:24:59.190] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003311)  
economic conditions.

**[02:25:00.510] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003312)  
But the direction of our

**[02:25:02.610] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003313)  
fiscal policy has remained

**[02:25:04.310] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003314)  
consistent. The administration

**[02:25:06.630] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003315)  
has remained committed to the path

**[02:25:08.570] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003316)  
of fiscal consolidation with

**[02:25:10.650] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003317)  
the goal of bringing down the

**[02:25:12.590] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003318)  
deficit-to-GDP ratio

**[02:25:14.330] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003319)  
from 5.4% this

**[02:25:16.590] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003320)  
year to just 3.5%

**[02:25:18.730] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003321)  
by 2030,

**[02:25:20.370] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003322)  
while supporting growth.

**[02:25:22.810] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003323)  
To stay the course amid

**[02:25:24.290] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003324)  
ongoing geopolitical tensions

**[02:25:26.610] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003325)  
and the need to fund the

**[02:25:28.490] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003326)  
government's priority programs,

**[02:25:30.510] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003327)  
without relying on new taxes,

**[02:25:33.170] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003328)  
we strengthened revenues.

**[02:25:35.310] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003329)  
Total revenues grew

**[02:25:36.630] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003330)  
double digits at an annual average

**[02:25:38.770] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003331)  
of 10.54%

**[02:25:40.790] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003332)  
over the last four years,

**[02:25:43.610] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003333)  
as tax revenues likewise

**[02:25:44.950] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003334)  
increased by an average of

**[02:25:46.350] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003335)  
10.47% over the same

**[02:25:48.930] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003336)  
period,

**[02:25:50.930] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003337)  
outpacing the growth of nominal

**[02:25:52.810] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003338)  
GDP of 9.6%.

**[02:25:55.950] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003339)  
And for the first time in its history,

**[02:25:59.690] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003340)  
in 2020,

**[02:26:00.510] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003341)  
the BIR surpassed

**[02:26:02.770] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003342)  
3 trillion pesos

**[02:26:03.930] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003343)  
in tax collections.

**[02:26:06.250] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003344)  
As we continue to stay the course

**[02:26:09.530] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003345)  
to meet our fiscal program for the year,

**[02:26:12.470] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003346)  
as of June

**[02:26:13.390] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003347)

**[02:28:56.610] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003429)

Those that strengthen

The objective is not to spend

**[02:29:10.750] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003436)

**[02:29:14.290] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003437)  
Because of these efforts,

**[02:29:16.290] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003438)

**[02:29:17.990] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003439)  
to narrow.

From 8.6% in 2021

**[02:29:22.290] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003441)  
and 7.3%

**[02:29:23.950] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003442)  
in 2022,

**[02:29:25.670] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003443)  
we have consistently brought down

**[02:29:27.670] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003444)  
the fiscal deficit to

**[02:29:29.590] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003445)  
6.2%

**[02:29:30.610] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003446)  
in 2023,

**[02:29:32.310] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003447)  
then to 5.7%,

**[02:29:34.150] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003448)  
and last year at 5.6%.

**[02:29:36.950] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003449)  
And as we continue to make

**[02:29:40.440] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003450)  
progress this 2026,

**[02:29:42.760] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003451)  
despite the economic shocks we have

**[02:29:44.340] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003452)  
faced, including those arising from the

**[02:29:46.220] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003453)  
conflict in the Middle East.

**[02:29:48.480] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003454)  
In the first half, our deficit

**[02:29:50.360] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003455)  
to GDP ratio improved

**[02:29:52.080] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003456)  
to 5.46%,

**[02:29:54.560] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003457)  
compared with

**[02:29:56.080] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003458)  
5.65% in the same

**[02:29:58.240] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003459)  
period last year.

**[02:30:00.000] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003460)  
and we remain on track to meet our fiscal deficit target for 2026.

**[02:30:05.220] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003461)  
We project a deficit-to-GDP ratio of 5.44% in the second half of 2026,

**[02:30:12.960] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003462)  
bringing the full-year ratio to 5.45%,

**[02:30:16.380] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003463)  
hopefully our lowest deficit-to-GDP ratio since the start of the administration.

**[02:30:23.460] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003464)  
This continued reduction in the deficit is an important indicator

**[02:30:27.140] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003465)  
that the fiscal discipline we are pursuing is translating into concrete results.

**[02:30:32.160] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003466)  
And because we continue to manage our fiscal deficit responsibly,

**[02:30:37.580] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003467)  
our debt levels remain sustainable.

**[02:30:42.800] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003468)  
In 2025, the national government debt stood at 63.2% of GDP,

**[02:30:48.500] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003469)  
while the general government debt finished at 56.8% of GDP,

**[02:30:53.120] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003470)  
well below the 70% international benchmark by the World Bank

**[02:30:57.500] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003471)  
for debt sustainability.

**[02:30:59.320] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003472)  
And within a manageable range compared to other emerging economies.

**[02:31:05.240] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003473)  
Just a point I'd like to raise or stress is that the definition of the 70% threshold

**[02:31:10.560] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003474)  
is based on general government debt, not national government debt to GDP.

**[02:31:19.130] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003475)  
More importantly, we have maintained a prudent debt mix,

**[02:31:22.430] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003476)  
predominantly domestic, predominantly carrying fixed interest rates,

**[02:31:26.850] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003477)  
and predominantly structured with long repayment terms.

**[02:31:31.590] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003478)  
First, 67% of our outstanding debt is domestic.

**[02:31:36.290] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003479)  
This reduces our exposure to foreign exchange risks,

**[02:31:39.390] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003480)  
while also supporting the continued development of our local capital market.

**[02:31:44.650] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003481)  
This has been the direction since the start of this administration.

**[02:31:48.810] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003482)  
Second, 90% of our debt carries fixed interest rates.

**[02:31:53.470] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003483)  
This provides greater certainty in our debt servicing costs

**[02:31:56.550] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003484)  
and shields us from sudden increases or fluctuations in global interest rates.

**[02:32:01.590] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003485)  
And third, 84.1% of our debt has long-term repayment periods,

**[02:32:09.750] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003486)  
meaning we have several years before these obligations fall due.

**[02:32:14.510] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003487)  
This strategic borrowing mix by our Bureau of Treasury

**[02:32:17.310] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003488)  
strengthens our resilience to external shocks

**[02:32:21.430] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003489)  
and makes our debt obligations more predictable and manageable over the long term.

**[02:32:27.390] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003490)  
As the global markets assessment of our fiscal fundamentals is also reflected,

**[02:32:32.770] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003491)  
it is also reflected in the confidence of international investors.

**[02:32:37.650] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003492)  
Our sovereign credit ratings remain at investment-grade levels.

**[02:32:41.890] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003493)  
We have two A- ratings from Japanese credit rating agencies

**[02:32:45.590] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003494)  
and the equivalent of BBB or BBB+, from the global rating agencies.

**[02:32:53.430] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003495)  
This reflects their continued confidence in the country's economic fundamentals

**[02:33:01.050] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003496)  
and our capacity to manage debt.

**[02:33:02.750] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003497)  
We are also confident that we can manage our public finances.

**[02:33:05.070] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003498)  
Just recently, R&I and Moody's affirmed the country's investment-grade credit ratings

**[02:33:11.730] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003499)  
with stable outlook.

**[02:33:13.770] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003500)  
This confirms our strong macroeconomic fundamentals

**[02:33:16.770] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003501)  
and that the reforms we've put in place are working.

**[02:33:20.810] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003502)  
Higher credit ratings reflect minimal default risk,

**[02:33:24.150] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003503)  
signaling lenders to offer lower interest rates.

**[02:33:27.690] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003504)  
When the country can borrow at lower interest rates,

**[02:33:30.330] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003505)  
private businesses and consumers can also borrow at lower interest rates.

**[02:33:32.530] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003506)  
We have also seen progress in our integration into global capital markets,

**[02:33:41.490] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003507)  
with the upcoming historic debut of our peso-denominated government bonds

**[02:33:47.650] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003508)  
in the JPMorgan's Government Bond Index Emerging Markets in January 2027.

**[02:33:54.610] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003509)  
This is significant because this is our first-ever inclusion in a major global bond index.

**[02:34:00.530] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003510)  
This reflects a

**[02:34:01.390] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003511)  
strong vote of

**[02:34:01.890] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003512)  
confidence in our

**[02:34:02.430] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003513)  
solid fundamentals and

**[02:34:03.250] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003514)  
fiscal discipline.

**[02:34:08.350] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003515)  
This will strengthen demand for Philippine government securities,

**[02:34:12.090] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003516)  
improve market liquidity,

**[02:34:13.830] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003517)  
support the development of our capital markets,

**[02:34:16.450] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003518)  
and help lower borrowing costs for the government overtime.

**[02:34:21.110] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003519)  
In 2027, we will project borrowing requirements to reach 3.3 trillion.

**[02:34:29.410] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003520)  
We will carry the same principles of our debt strategy

**[02:34:32.430] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003521)  
into our borrowing program and make it even more sustainable.

**[02:34:36.250] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003522)  
We are increasing the share of domestic borrowing to 72%,

**[02:34:39.950] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003523)  
which means about 2.4 trillion pesos will be sourced from the domestic market,

**[02:34:46.030] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003524)  
while the remaining 28% will come from external sources such as loans and global bonds.

**[02:34:52.910] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003525)  
This borrowing strategy allows us to keep the cost of borrowing low

**[02:34:56.770] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003526)  
while helping broaden our investor base,

**[02:35:00.110] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003527)  
maintain access to key international markets,

**[02:35:03.110] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003528)  
and support the continued development of our local bond market.

**[02:35:08.400] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003529)  
With tax collections projected to grow by an average of 9% annually from 2026 to 2028,

**[02:35:14.880] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003530)  
total revenues are targeted to reach 5.5 trillion pesos by the end of the President's term.

**[02:35:21.480] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003531)  
This means our revenue agencies will have to raise the bar even further.

**[02:35:25.760] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003532)  
The BIR and BOC will need to continue improving efficiency,

**[02:35:29.960] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003533)  
strengthening compliance,

**[02:35:30.880] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003534)  
and leveraging technology to sustain faster growth in collections.

**[02:35:35.820] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003535)  
Coupled with stronger collection efforts,

**[02:35:38.360] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003536)  
we are looking to pursue reforms that will make our revenue systems more efficient,

**[02:35:43.720] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003537)  
equitable, and sustainable.

**[02:35:46.200] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003538)  
We are promoting growth, revenue, and equity towards socio-economic sustainability or progress

**[02:35:54.480] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003539)  
through a comprehensive reform package that provides targeted tax relief

**[02:35:58.880] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003540)  
while strengthening revenues from

**[02:36:01.120] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003541)  
products with social, environmental, and

**[02:36:03.120] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003542)  
health costs.

**[02:36:06.120] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003543)  
We likewise expect more revenues from the proposed Multinational Minimum Tax Bill,

**[02:36:11.120] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003544)  
which will preserve our taxing rights and ensure the taxes arising from economic activity in the Philippines

**[02:36:17.120] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003545)  
are collected here.

**[02:36:20.120] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003546)  
And the General Tax Amnesty Bill mentioned by the President in his SONA

**[02:36:25.120] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003547)  
to encourage the settlement of outstanding tax obligations,

**[02:36:29.120] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003548)  
improve compliance,

**[02:36:30.240] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003549)  
and bring more taxpayers into the formal tax system.

**[02:36:35.240] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003550)  
Disbursements will grow moderately from 2026 to 2028.

**[02:36:40.600] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003551)  
We must be more deliberate where we put our resources.

**[02:36:44.520] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003552)  
Prioritize investments that strengthen our productive capacity,

**[02:36:48.480] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003553)  
support long-term growth,

**[02:36:49.720] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003554)  
and deliver tangible benefits to our people.

**[02:36:53.720] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003555)  
We must focus on programs and investments that

**[02:36:58.720] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003556)  
generate the greatest economic and social

**[02:36:59.920] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003557)  
returns, particularly in critical infrastructure, health, education, and other areas that support

**[02:37:07.140] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003558)  
long-term growth. As revenues grow faster than disbursements, we will see a clear and sustained

**[02:37:14.600] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003559)  
path towards fiscal consolidation. The deficit-to-GDP ratio is projected to steadily decline

**[02:37:21.840] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003560)  
from 5.4 percent in 2026 to 3.5 percent by 2030, putting us on a progressively stronger fiscal

**[02:37:32.700] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003561)  
footing. This improving fiscal trajectory is also reflected in our debt outlook. From 2026 to 2030,

**[02:37:40.800] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003562)  
both national government and general government debt ratios are projected to decrease.

**[02:37:46.760] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003563)  
NG debt is projected to ease from 65 percent to 63 percent in 2030,

**[02:37:52.260] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003564)  
and general government debt is expected to decline from 59 percent to 56 percent by 2030.

**[02:38:00.320] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003565)  
As we look ahead, the path we had laid out is clear. We assure the honorable members of this

**[02:38:06.380] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003566)  
chamber that the economic team will continue to strengthen revenues, manage expenditures

**[02:38:11.540] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003567)  
responsibly, reduce the deficit, and keep our debt on a sustainable path. At the same time,

**[02:38:18.760] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003568)  
we are building fiscal buffers that will give us room to respond to future shocks without compromising our long-term fiscal sustainability.

**[02:38:28.400] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003569)  
We look forward to working closely with the Senate to ensure that the government lives within its

**[02:38:35.600] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003570)  
means. This means making difficult choices, prioritizing programs and investments with

**[02:38:40.320] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003571)  
the greatest impact, and ensuring that new spending commitments are matched by sustainable

**[02:38:48.320] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003572)  
sources of funding. Fiscal discipline is not just about reducing the deficit.

**[02:38:53.360] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003573)  
More important is that we engage in smart spending. Our national budget can work harder

**[02:38:58.960] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003574)  
if we invest in programs and projects that can help shape our future. The government must continue

**[02:39:05.280] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003575)  
to address the immediate needs of our people, but we must look beyond the present and invest in high

**[02:39:11.280] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003576)  
multiplier programs and projects that create lasting economic value, those that create jobs,

**[02:39:17.120] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003577)  
raise incomes, and build a stronger economy tomorrow.

**[02:39:23.600] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003578)  
Well-chosen infrastructure, for example, does more than address today's needs. It can generate

**[02:39:28.800] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003579)  
economic activity, connect communities, attract private investment, and deliver benefits for many

**[02:39:34.320] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003580)  
years to come. Let us work together to make the 2027 national budget count and ensure that its

**[02:39:41.840] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-003581)  
benefits ripple through generations. This is the fiscal discipline we owe to the Filipino people. Maraming salamat po.

Next is Acting Secretary Kim De Leon. But how long is your presentation, Secretary De Leon?

**[02:40:15.800] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-003587)

**[02:40:21.840] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-003588)
