**[02:40:26.440] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003589)  
Thank you, Mr. Chair. To Senate President Win Gatchalian, Senate Finance Committee Chair J.V. Ejercito,

**[02:40:33.220] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003590)  
Honorable Members of the Senate Finance Committee and the Senate, my fellow economic managers and colleagues in government,

**[02:40:40.660] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003591)  
good morning. As Acting Secretary of the DBM and Chair of the DBCC, it is my honor to present to the Senate of the Philippines

**[02:40:49.580] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003592)  
the key dimensions and priorities.

**[02:40:51.840] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003593)  
of the fiscal year 2027 national expenditure program.

**[02:40:53.260] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003594)  
For fiscal year 2027, we are proposing a

**[02:40:57.160] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003595)  
7.2 trillion peso national budget

**[02:41:02.600] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003596)  
equivalent to 21.7%

**[02:41:06.880] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003597)  
of our country's gross domestic product.

**[02:41:12.360] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003598)  
This budget is 47 billion pesos or 6%

**[02:41:17.460] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003599)  
higher than the fiscal year 2026 GAA. Much of this increase is already accounted for

**[02:41:21.140] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003600)  
by mandatory expenditures and existing fiscal commitments by the government.

**[02:41:26.560] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003601)  
This includes higher national tax allotments for our local government units,

**[02:41:31.080] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003602)  
the fourth tranche of the salary adjustment for civilian government employees under EO64,

**[02:41:37.400] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003603)  
the corresponding salary increases for our military and uniformed personnel,

**[02:41:42.080] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003604)  
and other obligations that the government must honor.

**[02:41:45.360] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003605)  
We would like to highlight that the 6% increase in the overall budget

**[02:41:49.420] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003606)  
should not be interpreted to mean a uniform increase across agencies and programs.

**[02:41:55.180] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003607)  
Because limited fiscal space demands disciplined choices,

**[02:41:58.460] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003608)  
we prioritize programs and projects that are implementation-ready,

**[02:42:03.500] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003609)  
capable of delivering the greatest impact and offer the best value for every Filipino.

**[02:42:08.940] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003610)  
The P7.2 trillion budget before us, therefore, represents more than a spending ceiling.

**[02:42:15.920] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003611)  
It is the product of months of rigorous review to ensure that we will

**[02:42:19.400] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003612)  
meet the country's most urgent needs today, without compromising our capacity to meet the challenges of tomorrow.

**[02:42:27.840] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003613)  
The fiscal year 2027 national budget carries the theme

**[02:42:31.600] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003614)  
People-Centered Growth for an Inclusive and Resilient Future,

**[02:42:35.120] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003615)  
effectively capturing a simple but critical principle.

**[02:42:39.360] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003616)  
Economic progress must ultimately be measured by how it improves the lives of Filipinos.

**[02:42:45.120] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003617)  
We want growth that reaches communities,

**[02:42:47.160] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003618)  
creates opportunities across sectors and regions,

**[02:42:49.400] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003619)  
and strengthens our ability to

**[02:42:51.280] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003620)  
withstand future challenges.

**[02:42:54.220] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003621)  
But crafting a budget that would translate

**[02:42:54.960] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003622)  
this vision into reality requires more than

**[02:42:59.040] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003623)  
simply adding up agency requests.

**[02:43:02.940] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003624)  
When government agencies submitted more than

**[02:43:06.620] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003625)  
P11 trillion in budget proposals for possible inclusion in the NEP

**[02:43:11.680] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003626)  
we could not simply ask how much

**[02:43:13.600] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003627)  
each agency needs.

**[02:43:15.060] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003628)  
We had to ask harder

**[02:43:16.480] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003629)  
questions such as which programs are

**[02:43:19.040] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003630)  
ready to deliver, which will make the

**[02:43:21.520] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003631)  
greatest difference, and where will

**[02:43:23.600] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003632)  
every peso generate the greatest value

**[02:43:26.000] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003633)  
for the Filipino people?

**[02:43:27.940] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003634)  
These questions shaped the decisions behind this budget.

**[02:43:32.000] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003635)  
And throughout this process,

**[02:43:34.320] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003636)  
the President's direction was clear. Public resources must translate into

**[02:43:39.600] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003637)  
real and meaningful benefits for Filipinos across every region and community, through to the spirit

**[02:43:45.580] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003638)  
of our vision of Bawat Bayan Makikinabang. Beyond funding requirements, we also look closely at how

**[02:43:53.000] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003639)  
agencies have utilized the resources already entrusted to them. Their actual budget performance

**[02:43:59.280] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003640)  
and implementation capacity were key considerations in determining their allocations under the fiscal

**[02:44:05.380] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003641)  
year 2027 national budget. As of June 30, 2026, total available appropriations stood at 7.54 trillion

**[02:44:15.140] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003642)  
pesos.

**[02:44:15.580] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003643)  
Of this amount, 6.63 trillion pesos had been released as allotments to various agencies,

**[02:44:22.420] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003644)  
including 546.79 billion pesos from continuing fiscal year 2025 appropriations.

**[02:44:30.760] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003645)  
Agencies had obligated 3.29 trillion pesos, or about 49.5 percent, of released allotments,

**[02:44:38.440] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003646)  
comprising of 3.13 trillion from the current year appropriations and the remaining 158.58

**[02:44:45.480] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003647)  
billion from the current year appropriations.

**[02:44:45.580] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003648)  
Of the obligations reported, 81.9 percent had already been disbursed.

**[02:44:55.840] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003649)  
As of the same period, June 30, 2026, unreleased appropriations among

**[02:45:02.240] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003650)  
amounted to 820.21 billion from the current-year GAA and 89.7 billion from the 2025 continuing appropriations.

**[02:45:11.360] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003651)  
We would like to note that as of July 31, 2026, the DBM has released a total allotment of 6.18 trillion, equivalent to 91% of the program, leaving a balance of 610.95 billion pesos.

**[02:45:25.560] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003652)  
Of the 4.39 trillion program under the 2026 GAA, total allotments issued reached 3.85 trillion with a remaining balance of 537.32 billion pesos.

**[02:45:40.140] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003653)  
This balance includes 315.9 billion pertaining to agency-specific budgets and 221.41 billion under special purpose funds.

**[02:45:50.680] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003654)  
These indicators help us assess whether additional resources can be used.

**[02:45:55.560] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003655)  
The DBM will continue working closely with the agencies to improve their execution of their budget because the true measure of a budget is not simply how much is approved or released, but how effectively these resources become real results for our people.

**[02:46:16.860] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003656)  
Now, allow me to provide updates on the national government's disbursements for fiscal years 2025 to 2025.

**[02:46:25.560] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003657)  
NG disbursement in 2025 reached 6.03 trillion pesos, equivalent to 21.5% of GDP.

**[02:46:34.980] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003658)  
This was mainly driven by PS expenditures for salaries and benefits of government workforce such as education and health sectors, including the military and uniformed personnel.

**[02:46:46.540] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003659)  
MOOE also contributed strongly to the government's spending performance, owing to the implementation of social protection programs, agricultural services, and the development of a new government.

**[02:46:55.560] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003660)  
As well as the general operations of the government.

**[02:46:59.380] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003661)  
Meanwhile, disbursements are projected to increase by 7% on the average this year in 2027, reaching 6.466 trillion this year and 6.901 trillion next year.

**[02:47:12.620] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003662)  
Spending will continue to be supported by PS expenditures, reflective of the higher salaries of civilian government employees and higher base pay and subsistence allowance of MUPs.

**[02:47:24.640] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003663)  
As well as the general operations of the government.

**[02:47:25.540] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003664)  
As well as the requirements for creation and filling up of positions in various departments, particularly in education and health.

**[02:47:33.600] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003665)  
Both MOOE and infrastructure expenditures will remain significant to fund priority human capital development programs and flagship infrastructure projects, respectively.

**[02:47:44.080] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003666)  
The overall support to local government units will also continue to be substantial, driven by larger NTA shares, annual block grant to the BARM,

**[02:47:54.460] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003667)  
and annual financial support to the NTA.

**[02:47:55.160] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003668)  
The proposed financial assistance through the local government support fund.

**[02:47:58.820] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003669)  
Moving forward with the dimensions of the 2027 National Budget.

**[02:48:03.440] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003670)  
The proposed 2027 National Budget is composed of two main sources.

**[02:48:09.140] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003671)  
Programmed appropriations amount to 4.494 trillion pesos

**[02:48:13.660] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003672)  
and will finance the priority programs, projects, and operations of government.

**[02:48:19.600] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003673)  
Automatic appropriations total 2.706 trillion pesos

**[02:48:24.000] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003674)  
and will cover...

**[02:48:25.160] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003675)  
expenditures already mandated by existing laws. Major automatic appropriations include 1.32

**[02:48:32.740] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003676)  
trillion peso for the national tax allotment of LGUs, 1.114 trillion pesos for interest payments,

**[02:48:41.240] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003677)  
104.2 billion pesos for the annual block grant of the BARM, and 89 billion pesos for the retirement

**[02:48:48.160] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003678)  
and life insurance premiums of national government employees. This demonstrates that a considerable

**[02:48:54.640] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003679)  
portion of the 7.2 trillion peso budget is already determined by laws, formulas, and existing

**[02:49:01.740] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003680)  
obligations before government even begins deciding which new or expanded programs to fund.

**[02:49:08.600] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003681)  
We have likewise brought and programmed the appropriations down substantially to 112 billion

**[02:49:15.420] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003682)  
pesos. Nominally, this is the lowest proposed UA in the NEP since 2019, while its 1.56 percent

**[02:49:24.400] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003683)  
share is the lowest in the U.S.

**[02:49:24.640] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003684)  
share of the total expenditure program is the lowest ratio since 1991. Allow me to reiterate

**[02:49:31.880] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003685)  
that unprogrammed appropriations are not automatically available for spending. It is a

**[02:49:37.120] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003686)  
standby spending authority for specifically identified purposes that may be accessed only

**[02:49:43.380] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003687)  
when the funding conditions prescribed by law are satisfied. For fiscal year 2027,

**[02:49:49.540] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003688)  
the unprogrammed appropriations have been deliberately limited primarily to

**[02:49:54.640] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003689)  
partially finance the restoration of the fund balance previously remitted by the PDIC and to

**[02:50:00.920] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003690)  
support foreign-assisted projects that are still undergoing assessment and evaluation by the

**[02:50:07.040] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003691)  
Investment Coordination Committee and require approval by the ED Council. By keeping standby

**[02:50:13.200] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003692)  
appropriations to the minimum necessary, the administration is placing more expenditures

**[02:50:18.980] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003693)  
under programmed appropriations, thereby strengthening expenditure planning,

**[02:50:24.640] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003694)  
and ensuring the timely implementation of priority programs and projects. By expense class,

**[02:50:31.480] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003695)  
the proposed budget reflects our commitment to sustaining government operations while directing

**[02:50:37.040] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003696)  
resources toward investments with lasting economic and social returns. MOOE amounts to 2.944

**[02:50:44.760] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003697)  
trillion pesos. Notably, MOOE declines by 36.2 billion or 1.2 percent from 2026 level,

**[02:50:54.360] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003698)  
even if the budget is not enough to support the development of the government. So,

**[02:50:54.620] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003699)  
MOOE is not enough to support the development of the government. So, MOOE is not enough to support the development of the government. So,

**[02:50:54.640] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003700)  
MOOE is not enough to support the development of the government. So, MOOE is not enough to support the development of the government. So,

**[02:50:54.700] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003701)  
MOOE is not enough to support the development of the government. So, MOOE is not enough to support the development of the government. So,

**[02:50:54.800] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003702)  
as the total national budget increases by 6 percent. This indicates that the overall budget growth is not being driven by a broad expansion of operating expenditures.

**[02:51:06.620] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003703)  
PS will receive 1.982 trillion up by 138.2 billion or 7.5 percent. This will support public servants who will deliver education,

**[02:51:17.720] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003704)  
healthcare, public safety, national defense, and other essential services, while also providing for salary adjustments,

**[02:51:24.620] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003705)  
and personal requirements already committed by the government.

**[02:51:28.740] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003706)  
We would like to emphasize that both PS and MOOE remain fully covered by our projected revenues.

**[02:51:37.580] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003707)  
Meanwhile, capital outlays increased to 1.16 trillion pesos,

**[02:51:42.600] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003708)  
an increase of 140.8 billion or 13.8% to finance infrastructure, facilities, equipment, and other productive assets.

**[02:51:53.340] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003709)  
Financial expenses amount to 1.114 trillion pesos, up by 164.3 billion or 17.3% largely due to interest payments.

**[02:52:05.420] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003710)  
Nevertheless, we affirm that our debt remains manageable as debt servicing is explicitly provided for in the budget.

**[02:52:13.220] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003711)  
Our approach is not to pursue deficit reduction at the expense of growth.

**[02:52:17.120] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003712)  
Instead, we are advancing a strategic and gradual fiscal consolidation path

**[02:52:22.560] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003713)  
that supports the development of a new economy.

**[02:52:23.320] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003714)  
This safeguards our obligations and fiscal credibility while preserving the investments needed to strengthen our people and sustain our economic growth.

**[02:52:33.720] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003715)  
Across the five sectors of the proposed budget, social services will continue to receive the largest share at 2.456 trillion or 34.1%.

**[02:52:44.440] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003716)  
This will directly support education, health, social protection, employment, housing, and other services that affect the everyday lives of people.

**[02:52:53.320] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003717)  
Economic services will receive 1.833 trillion or 25.5% for infrastructure, agriculture, transportation, water resources, digital connectivity, and other investments that improve productivity.

**[02:53:09.760] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003718)  
General public services account for 1.317 trillion or 18.3%, while defense will receive 452.4 billion or 6.3%.

**[02:53:20.920] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003719)  
Debt burden accounts for 1.13 trillion or 15.9%, covering interest payments and net lending to government corporations.

**[02:53:21.680] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003720)  
Public services will receive 1.317 trillion or 18.3%, while defense will receive 452.4 billion or 6.3%.

**[02:53:22.720] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003721)  
while defense will receive 452.4 billion or 6.3%.

**[02:53:23.220] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003722)  
While defense will receive 452.4 billion or 6.3%.

**[02:53:23.320] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003723)  
or 15.9%, covering interest payments and net lending to government corporations.

**[02:53:31.340] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003724)  
Honoring these obligations protect the government's creditworthiness

**[02:53:34.940] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003725)  
and helps preserve access to financing for future investments.

**[02:53:39.720] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003726)  
Our task is to maintain that balance, honoring our government's obligations

**[02:53:44.100] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003727)  
while continuing to fund what our people need.

**[02:53:47.520] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003728)  
By recipient units, national government agencies will receive 4.332 trillion,

**[02:53:54.340] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003729)  
the largest share of the budget.

**[02:53:56.460] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003730)  
However, their allocation grows by only 4.5%, below the overall budget growth of 6%,

**[02:54:03.500] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003731)  
reflecting continued restraint in national government spending.

**[02:54:08.020] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003732)  
Local government units will receive 1.533 trillion, including a 1.32 trillion NTA,

**[02:54:14.940] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003733)  
compared with around 1.1 million NTA.

**[02:54:17.520] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003734)  
This means roughly 129.3 billion more, or about 11%,

**[02:54:24.920] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003735)  
will flow directly to LGUs to support devolved functions and frontline services.

**[02:54:31.480] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003736)  
GOCCs will receive 220.5 billion, while 1.114 trillion will go to interest payments.

**[02:54:39.480] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003737)  
These allocations underscore an important feature of the 2027 budget.

**[02:54:44.320] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003738)  
Resources are not concentrated solely at the national level,

**[02:54:47.520] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003739)  
a substantial share is transferred to LGUs,

**[02:54:51.400] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003740)  
bringing our country's resources closer to the communities

**[02:54:54.520] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003741)  
where many essential public services are delivered to our citizens.

**[02:54:59.680] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003742)  
The same principle is also evident in the regional distribution of the budget.

**[02:55:04.560] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003743)  
Of the proposed 7.2 trillion, 4.603 trillion, or 63.9%,

**[02:55:10.520] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003744)  
is directly attributable to the regions.

**[02:55:13.360] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003745)  
The national capital region accounts for 1.112,

**[02:55:17.520] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003746)  
Luzon at 1.659 trillion,

**[02:55:20.480] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003747)  
Visayas at 4.8 billion,

**[02:55:23.780] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003748)  
and Mindanao at 1.088 trillion.

**[02:55:26.400] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003749)  
The remaining 2.597 trillion, or 36.1%, is non-regionalized,

**[02:55:33.320] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003750)  
consisting of 1.983 trillion pesos in nationwide allocations

**[02:55:38.760] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003751)  
and 613.8 billion in central office allocations.

**[02:55:44.920] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003752)  
We would like to clarify,

**[02:55:46.440] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003753)  
the important distinction of nationwide from Metro Manila.

**[02:55:50.640] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003754)  
Nationwide allocations pertain to funds that are still to be distributed

**[02:55:54.720] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003755)  
to various regions of the departments and agencies,

**[02:55:58.960] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003756)  
as this cannot yet be geographically assigned at the time the NEP was prepared.

**[02:56:04.360] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003757)  
Ultimately, the majority of the budget is intended to reach our regions and communities.

**[02:56:09.940] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003758)  
That is what we mean when we say,

**[02:56:11.720] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003759)  
bawat bayan makikinabang.

**[02:56:14.600] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003760)  
With the overall framework,

**[02:56:16.080] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003761)  
and priorities of the budget established,

**[02:56:18.560] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003762)  
let us now turn to where our most significant investments will be directed,

**[02:56:22.640] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003763)  
and how this will translate into better outcomes for Filipinos.

**[02:56:27.220] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003764)  
Education remains at the center of our investment in human capital.

**[02:56:31.660] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003765)  
The Department of Education will receive the highest allocation at 975.96 billion pesos,

**[02:56:38.700] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003766)  
while 176.5 billion is provided for higher education

**[02:56:44.040] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003767)  
to broaden access to quality,

**[02:56:46.520] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003768)  
and affordable tertiary learning.

**[02:56:49.020] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003769)  
Taken together with the other components of government education spending,

**[02:56:53.200] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003770)  
our proposed investment in basic and higher education reaches 1.326 trillion,

**[02:57:00.360] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003771)  
equivalent to nearly 4% of the GDP,

**[02:57:03.880] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003772)  
and effectively reaching the lower bound of the UNESCO Education 2030 benchmark

**[02:57:09.140] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003773)  
of 4-6% of GDP for education spending for the second time.

**[02:57:15.080] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003774)  
The difference between the two is that, for the first time,

**[02:57:16.060] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003775)  
between 1.314 trillion reflected in the President's budget and the 1.326 trillion presented during the DBCC briefing at the House

**[02:57:26.060] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003776)  
is due to the inclusion of the Tier 2 projections for BARM education agencies which were not yet available when the budget message was prepared and printed.

**[02:57:36.240] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003777)  
By the time of the House briefing, these projections were already available and were therefore included in computing the overall education sector figure.

**[02:57:46.060] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003778)  
So, to be clear, there was no change in the 2027 NEP after its submission.

**[02:57:51.700] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003779)  
The difference simply reflects the more complete BARM education sector figures,

**[02:57:56.840] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003780)  
which is available at the time of the DBCC presentation.

**[02:58:00.460] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003781)  
This is consistent with how we view education as a national commitment,

**[02:58:04.640] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003782)  
one that leaves no learner behind, whether served by our national education agencies, in BARM, and in all communities across the country.

**[02:58:14.980] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003783)  
More importantly,

**[02:58:16.060] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003784)  
these allocations translate into specific investments.

**[02:58:20.560] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003785)  
We are proposing 12.09 billion for the expanded career progression system for public school teachers,

**[02:58:27.720] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003786)  
an increase of almost 6 billion or 96.6% from the current year.

**[02:58:32.960] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003787)  
This is to support the reclassification and career advancement of our teachers.

**[02:58:37.260] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003788)  
Another 10.36 billion allocation next year will also sustain the 10,000 peso teaching allowance under the Kabalika,

**[02:58:46.900] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003789)  
For tertiary education,

**[02:58:49.660] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003790)  
61.1 billion is provided for the universal access to quality tertiary education across state universities and colleges,

**[02:58:59.160] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003791)  
CHED and TESDA,

**[02:59:00.680] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003792)  
supporting free higher education, tertiary education subsidies,

**[02:59:05.520] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003793)  
and free technical vocational education.

**[02:59:08.700] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003794)  
Ultimately,

**[02:59:09.700] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003795)  
the significance of the 1.326 trillion peso budget

**[02:59:13.620] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003796)  
will not be measured by the amount of education.

**[02:59:15.620] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003797)  
This is to support the development of the education sector,

**[02:59:15.700] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003798)  
and to support the development of the education sector.

**[02:59:15.760] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003799)  
It will be measured by better learning outcomes, better supported teachers, wider access to education and training, and more opportunities for Filipino learners to build a future they rightfully deserve.

**[02:59:31.760] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003800)  
The top 10 departments with the largest allocations account for 51.4% of the proposed budget.

**[02:59:38.900] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003801)  
Apart from education, major allocations will go to public works and highways, health, interior and local government, national defense, transportation, agriculture, social welfare and development, higher education, and the judiciary, fully aligned with the administration's priorities and the Philippine development.

**[03:00:03.040] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003802)  
On infrastructure, let me emphasize that infrastructure is more than just the DPWH budget. Under the Build Better More infrastructure program, the government is proposing 1.467 trillion pesos, equivalent to 4.4% of GDP for infrastructure in 2027.

**[03:00:21.980] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003803)  
These investments are distributed across public works, transportation, agriculture, education, defense, health, digital infrastructure, and other sectors.

**[03:00:34.760] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003804)  
Specifically, DPWH will receive 643.95 billion, or the second largest allocation among agencies.

**[03:00:44.000] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003805)  
This is partly to support ongoing locally funded and foreign-assisted infrastructure flagship projects.

**[03:00:50.680] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003806)  
Major projects include the Laguna Lakeshore Road Network Project at 35 billion, Bataan-Cavite Interlink Bridge Project at 22 billion, Davao City Bypass Construction Project Package 1 at 11.9 billion,

**[03:01:05.480] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003807)  
Cebu-Mactan Bridge and Coastal Road Construction Project at 8.5 billion, and Pasig-Marikina River Channel Improvement Project Phase 4 at 8.5 billion pesos.

**[03:01:17.220] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003808)  
Transportation is likewise a major priority.

**[03:01:20.680] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003809)  
With 300.96 billion proposed for the DOTR and its attached agencies.

**[03:01:26.400] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003810)  
This includes 123.84 billion for the North-South Commuter Railway System, 67.44 billion for Phase 1 of the Metro Manila Subway Project, and 1.94 billion for the MRT Line 3 Rehabilitation Project.

**[03:01:45.160] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003811)  
Beyond Metro Manila,

**[03:01:47.320] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003812)  
175.49 million is provided for the Cebu Bus Rapid Transit Project, and 15.08 billion for the Davao Public Transport Modernization Project.

**[03:01:50.680] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003813)  
We are also investing 8.99 billion in the new Cebu International Container Port Project, and 1.41 billion in the new Dumaguete Airport Development Project.

**[03:02:11.880] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003814)  
These investments demonstrate that reducing travel time and logistics costs, connecting regional economies,

**[03:02:19.700] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003815)  
improving the movement of people and goods, and bringing more Filipinos within reach of jobs and economic opportunities are important priorities of this administration.

**[03:02:31.900] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003816)  
Our other major investments pursue the same objective of improving people's security and quality of life.

**[03:02:39.280] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003817)  
Across the agriculture sector, 261.7 billion will support food security, productivity, and the livelihood.

**[03:02:49.700] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003818)  
The proposed fiscal year 2027 budget continues to make quality healthcare more accessible, more affordable, and more responsive to the needs of every Filipino by allocating 353.8 billion for the health sector.

**[03:03:10.160] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003819)  
We are providing 107.29 billion for the operations of DOH regional hospitals and other health facilities.

**[03:03:19.700] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003820)  
Along with 28.19 billion for DOH hospitals and Metro Manila to expand healthcare capacity, modernize facilities, and strengthen specialized medical services.

**[03:03:33.000] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003821)  
This means more Filipinos can access quality healthcare closer to home, while those requiring highly specialized treatment continue to receive world-class care in our major public hospitals.

**[03:03:45.920] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003822)  
To further reduce what Filipino families,

**[03:03:49.700] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003823)  
from out of their own pockets when they are hospitalized,

**[03:03:53.780] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003824)  
we are strengthening the implementation of the universal healthcare through PhilHealth

**[03:03:57.980] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003825)  
with an allocation of 74.45 billion pesos.

**[03:04:03.000] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003826)  
This will support the continued expansion of the PhilHealth's benefit packages,

**[03:04:08.300] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003827)  
including the implementation of zero-balance billing in both DOH and LGU hospitals.

**[03:04:14.080] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003828)  
From only six LGU hospitals this year,

**[03:04:18.580] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003829)  
zero-balance billing will expand to 352 LGU hospitals nationwide next year,

**[03:04:26.600] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003830)  
allowing millions more Filipinos to receive quality hospital care without worrying about the cost.

**[03:04:33.940] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003831)  
More importantly, this means that when illness strikes,

**[03:04:37.700] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003832)  
Filipino families can focus on their loved ones' recovery,

**[03:04:40.880] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003833)  
not on how they will pay the hospital bill.

**[03:04:44.080] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003834)  
This is our commitment to making quality healthcare more accessible,

**[03:04:48.200] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003835)  
more affordable, and more compassionate to every Filipino.

**[03:04:52.360] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003836)  
For social protection, DSWD will receive 241 billion,

**[03:04:58.140] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003837)  
including 99 billion for the implementation of the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program.

**[03:05:04.540] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003838)  
For national defense, 328.8 billion is proposed,

**[03:05:09.700] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003839)  
including 50 billion for the revised AFP modernization program

**[03:05:14.080] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003840)  
and 10 billion higher than the current year's level.

**[03:05:17.720] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003841)  
The Philippine Coast Guard will receive 45.51 billion,

**[03:05:22.760] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003842)  
while 73.67 billion is proposed for the subsistence allowance

**[03:05:28.060] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003843)  
of our military and uniformed personnel across concerned agencies.

**[03:05:33.840] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003844)  
For the judiciary, 86.27 billion is included

**[03:05:38.380] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003845)  
to support the administration of justice and access to judicial services.

**[03:05:43.340] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003846)  
Consistent with the constitutional principle of judicial independence

**[03:05:47.800] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003847)  
and the provisions of the Judiciary Fiscal Autonomy Act,

**[03:05:52.640] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003848)  
the Supreme Court's original budget proposal has been incorporated into the fiscal year 2027 NEP,

**[03:06:00.440] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003849)  
recognizing the judiciary's fiscal autonomy and constitutional mandate.

**[03:06:06.300] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003850)  
Resilience is likewise integral to the 2027 budget.

**[03:06:10.240] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003851)  
We are proposing 45.67 billion,

**[03:06:13.340] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003852)  
including 14.67 billion for the Disaster Rehabilitation and Reconstruction Assistance Program for LGUs and 1 billion for the People's Survival Fund.

**[03:06:30.780] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003853)  
Taken together, these investments reveal the broader purpose of the 2027 budget

**[03:06:36.000] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003854)  
to protect vulnerable Filipinos, strengthen human capital and food security,

**[03:06:40.980] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003855)  
build productive infrastructure,

**[03:06:43.340] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003856)  
safeguard the nation,

**[03:06:45.100] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003857)  
empower our region,

**[03:06:46.640] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003858)  
and improve our ability to withstand future shocks.

**[03:06:50.640] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003859)  
That commitment extends directly to our local government units.

**[03:06:54.240] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003860)  
1.32 trillion NTA gives LGUs greater resources to perform devolved functions,

**[03:07:02.040] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003861)  
while 115.62 billion will support peace, self-governance,

**[03:07:08.200] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003862)  
and long-term development in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao.

**[03:07:13.340] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003863)  
We are likewise proposing 58.53 billion for the Local Government Support Fund,

**[03:07:19.360] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003864)  
covering financial assistance to LGUs, the Growth Equity Fund, and the Barangay Development Program.

**[03:07:25.580] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003865)  
By strengthening local fiscal capacity, we bring resources and decision-making closer to communities

**[03:07:32.700] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003866)  
and give every region a stronger voice in national development.

**[03:07:37.440] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003867)  
This is what people-centered growth means, one that reaches every community,

**[03:07:42.100] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003868)  
creates opportunities

**[03:07:43.340] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003869)  
for every Filipino,

**[03:07:44.920] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003870)  
and ensures that progress is broadly and fairly shared across the country.

**[03:07:50.940] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003871)  
These are only some of the key priorities reflected in the proposed Fiscal Year 2027 National Budget.

**[03:07:57.420] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003872)  
To provide a broader view of the programs and projects we seek to pursue,

**[03:08:02.580] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003873)  
we have also prepared a short video presentation that we can probably share later.

**[03:08:07.440] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003874)  
Mr. Senate President, Mr. Chairperson, and Honorable Members of the Senate,

**[03:08:11.800] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003875)  
the National Expenditure Program,

**[03:08:13.340] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003876)  
before you represents the Executive's best judgment

**[03:08:17.360] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003877)  
of how limited public resources can respond to the country's immediate needs

**[03:08:22.720] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003878)  
while protecting our long-term fiscal and development goals.

**[03:08:27.240] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003879)  
But we also recognize that budget-making process does not end with the submission of the NEP.

**[03:08:32.660] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003880)  
The scrutiny of Congress is an essential part of that process.

**[03:08:36.900] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003881)  
The questions you will raise, the programs you examine,

**[03:08:40.000] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003882)  
and the choices we make together will ultimately,

**[03:08:43.340] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003883)  
We will determine whether the national budget is able to deliver what our people expect from government. On the part of the DBM and the Development Budget Coordination Committee, we come before the Senate prepared to explain our assumptions, account for our recommendations, and engage constructively throughout the deliberations.

**[03:09:01.960] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003884)  
Because behind every number we discuss in this hearing is a consequence beyond these halls, a classroom that may be built, a hospital patient who may receive care, a farmer who may gain better access to markets, a community protected from disaster, or a Filipino family given a better opportunity to move forward.

**[03:09:24.880] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003885)  
That is the standard by which this budget should ultimately be judged, not simply by how much government spends.

**[03:09:31.960] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003886)  
But by how much better government is able to serve.

**[03:09:36.020] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003887)  
We therefore look forward to working with the Senate toward a fiscal year 2027 national budget that is disciplined in its choices, credible in its commitments, transparent in its use, and meaningful in the lives of our people.

**[03:09:51.400] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-003888)  
Maraming salamat po.

**[03:09:53.120] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-003889)  
Okay, thank you, Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon.

**[03:09:57.800] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-003890)  
Before we take a short break, the chair would like to acknowledge.

**[03:10:01.960] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-003891)  
So we'll take a very quick lunch break.

**[03:10:07.420] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-003892)  
We resume at 1.35 p.m.

Malaki.

**[04:14:49.680] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004311)

**[04:14:53.680] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004312)

**[04:14:54.680] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004313)

**[04:14:56.680] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004314)

**[04:15:00.000] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004315)

**[04:15:11.300] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004316)

**[04:15:19.560] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004318)

**[04:15:32.460] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004320)

**[04:15:36.320] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004321)

**[04:15:45.960] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004322)  
So bakit ang sagot dati ng, hindi naman kayo, no, yung previous,

**[04:15:50.280] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004323)

**[04:15:55.300] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004324)

**[04:15:57.280] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004325)

**[04:16:00.600] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004326)

**[04:16:06.280] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004327)

**[04:16:10.620] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004328)

**[04:16:14.860] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004329)

**[04:16:19.060] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004330)

**[04:16:25.040] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004331)  
Kasi simple lang naman eh.

**[04:16:27.280] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004332)

**[04:16:32.840] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004333)  
So anyway, yung budgetary change in cash.

**[04:16:48.420] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004334)

**[04:16:50.520] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004335)  
May mga negative.

**[04:16:52.000] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004336)  
Kindly, for my continuing education, kindly clarify.

**[04:16:57.220] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004337)  
Also for the benefit of my other colleagues.

**[04:17:03.900] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004338)  
Budgetary change in cash.

**[04:17:07.060] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004339)  
Paki-explain lang.

**[04:17:08.380] Treasurer of the Philippines Sharon P. Almanza** (asr-004340)  
Thank you, Mr. Chair.

**[04:17:11.680] Treasurer of the Philippines Sharon P. Almanza** (asr-004341)  
It's basically the difference between our gross borrowing and net financing, Mr. Chair.

**[04:17:18.040] Treasurer of the Philippines Sharon P. Almanza** (asr-004342)  
Which means that if it's positive, then we borrowed for basically cash buffer.

**[04:17:24.140] Treasurer of the Philippines Sharon P. Almanza** (asr-004343)  
And then if it's negative, it means that we're using our cash buffer,

**[04:17:29.300] Treasurer of the Philippines Sharon P. Almanza** (asr-004344)  
basically financial asset, to cover the difference between the gross borrowing and the net financing.

**[04:17:35.820] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004345)  
Thank you.

**[04:17:39.280] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004346)  
Okay, moving on.

**[04:17:50.380] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004349)

**[04:17:55.500] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004350)

**[04:19:13.040] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004368)

**[04:20:21.200] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004382)

**[04:20:49.900] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004389)

**[04:21:26.680] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004396)

**[04:21:37.680] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004397)

**[04:21:38.740] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004398)

**[04:21:42.580] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004399)

**[04:21:48.260] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004400)

**[04:21:57.500] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004401)  
Parang for humanitarian.

**[04:21:59.760] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004402)

**[04:22:11.080] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004403)  
Mr. Chair, Your Honor,

**[04:22:14.050] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004404)

**[04:22:19.430] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004405)

**[04:22:22.170] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004406)

**[04:22:32.470] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004407)

**[04:22:40.370] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004408)

**[04:22:44.270] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004409)  
Meaning abolition, merger, or any possible action for the GOCC.

**[04:22:49.210] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004410)  
Your Honor, Mr. Chair, if I may, now that I'm looking at the list of non-performing GOCCs as a sample,

**[04:22:56.070] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004411)  
in fact, I'm very much aware of some of these GOCCs coming back to us when we submitted the NEP and was asking for more.

**[04:23:04.350] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004412)

**[04:23:12.770] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004414)

**[04:23:19.650] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004415)

**[04:23:26.750] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004416)

**[04:23:28.430] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004417)  
Yes, Your Honor.

**[04:23:31.940] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004418)  
Okay, yung regionalized budget against the national.

**[04:23:42.660] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004420)

**[04:24:05.600] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004425)

**[04:24:19.420] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004428)

**[04:24:44.720] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004437)

**[04:24:48.580] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004438)

**[04:24:52.680] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004439)

**[04:25:05.780] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004441)  
Yung actual.

**[04:25:06.400] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004442)

**[04:25:12.400] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004443)

**[04:25:12.900] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004444)

**[04:25:21.340] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004447)

**[04:25:27.080] Senator Panfilo Lacson** (asr-004448)

**[04:25:40.400] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004451)

**[04:25:43.540] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004452)

**[04:25:52.760] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004453)

**[04:26:00.100] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004454)

**[04:26:09.020] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004455)

**[04:26:12.460] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004456)

**[04:26:13.540] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004457)

**[04:26:19.320] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004458)

**[04:26:25.120] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004459)

**[04:26:31.720] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004460)

so that we can still deliver.

**[04:40:29.550] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004630)  
Even better services, whether these are for health, for education, for social protection,

**[04:40:38.410] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004631)  
even as we are constrained with the total amount.

**[04:40:43.070] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004632)  
I guess, I think this is very important moving forward that when we borrow,

**[04:40:51.530] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004633)  
and which will result in interest payments later,

**[04:40:54.970] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004634)  
we do make sure that what we borrowed is invested, is used properly,

**[04:40:59.550] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004635)  
so that it generates much higher value than what we pay later on

**[04:41:06.370] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004636)  
in terms of interest payments and amortization.

**[04:41:09.790] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004637)  
But I guess if the experience in the last three quarters,

**[04:41:14.190] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004638)  
or what we have seen in the scandals,

**[04:41:15.950] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004639)  
is that we have borrowed, put them in places where they didn't seem to contribute

**[04:41:23.510] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004640)  
to higher capacity for the economy,

**[04:41:26.950] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004641)  
then that's really the wrong and inefficient way of using financing.

**[04:41:36.090] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004642)  
Before I give way for the interjection of the chair,

**[04:41:40.770] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004643)  
precisely, may mga corrections talaga na kailangan namin gagawin dito sa proposed budget.

**[04:41:48.450] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004644)  
Scandals aside, at tinututukan din niya ng Senate, pero a much better budget pa po.

**[04:41:54.390] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004645)  
Mr. Chair?

**[04:41:55.750] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-004646)  
Yes, we need to have just...

**[04:41:56.950] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-004647)  
Senator Diveros, I'll try to interject.

**[04:41:59.610] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-004648)  
Same point po, the DBCC can answer, of course.

**[04:42:03.590] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-004649)  
At one point, does DBCC consider itong interest expenditure a serious constraint on development spending?

**[04:42:15.390] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-004650)  
Parang ano na tayo lagi, parang we're always looking at itong ating financial standing, debt servicing,

**[04:42:24.130] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-004651)  
to the point na parang we are already sacrificing.

**[04:42:26.950] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-004652)  
And development spending.

**[04:42:30.030] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-004653)  
Anybody can answer?

**[04:42:31.790] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-004654)  
Parang isa ka talaga bali sa akin, or...

**[04:42:36.420] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-004655)  
If I may, for me, from a development perspective, Mr. Chair,

**[04:42:45.660] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-004656)  
it doesn't hurt to pay interest payments if the amount we borrowed was able to generate far more incomes

**[04:42:57.500] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-004657)  
than the interest payments.

**[04:42:59.380] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-004658)  
And amortization that we paid for.

**[04:43:04.160] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-004659)  
So, ganun lang ho.

**[04:43:05.980] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-004660)  
So, we incur interest payments, and those interest payments can rise, but if we are able to guarantee

**[04:43:12.600] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-004661)  
that those yield better results for the economy, then that should not be a concern.

**[04:43:19.180] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-004662)  
So, we have not become too focused naman on keeping our finances in order, that we have

**[04:43:23.620] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-004663)  
under-invested in infrastructure, kasi parang nahuli na tayo eh.

**[04:43:27.420] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-004664)  
We're just spending on average...

**[04:43:29.380] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-004665)  
We're just spending on average of 2% through the how many decades as compared to our ASEAN

**[04:43:35.880] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-004666)  
neighbors who are spending 5% or more.

**[04:43:38.100] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-004667)  
Diba?

**[04:43:38.340] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-004668)  
Parang tayo nasa 2%.

**[04:43:39.700] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-004669)  
So, but now, a little bit higher, tumaas ng 6%.

**[04:43:44.080] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-004670)  
Previous administration, bumaba na naman ngayon.

**[04:43:47.240] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-004671)  
So, yun lang ang concern natin.

**[04:43:50.700] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-004672)  
Probably later on my timeline, I would just pursue this.

**[04:43:55.000] Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito** (asr-004673)  
So, Tertuberas, please continue.

**[04:43:57.160] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004674)  
Salamat, Mr. Chair.

**[04:43:58.320] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004675)  
So, moving up to...

**[04:43:59.380] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004676)  
To SECGO, yung debt ng bansa natin ngayon, 19.07 trillion pesos.

**[04:44:09.160] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004677)  
At lambas na po ito sa end of year, 2026 targets, at nasa Agosto pa lang po tayo.

**[04:44:16.140] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004678)  
So, maaari nyo po bang i-detalye kung aling mga agency programs ang nabawasan

**[04:44:22.560] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004679)  
ng mga budgets dahil sa lumiit na fiscal space natin ngayong taon?

**[04:44:27.680] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004680)  
Or bawat taon?

**[04:44:29.380] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004681)  
Mr. Chair.

**[04:44:30.700] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004682)  
Mr. Chair, Your Honor, I'm confirming that our total debt today is 19 trillion pesos.

**[04:44:36.060] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004683)  
But when it comes to the budget, I would have to defer to my colleague from the DBM to answer.

**[04:44:42.660] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004684)  
Before we move, Mr. Chair, to Secde Leon, would the Secretary like to comment on how can we call this a people-centered budget?

**[04:44:51.020] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004685)  
Kung mga one-seventh ng budget ay gagastusin natin sa debt interest payments pa lamang.

**[04:44:58.440] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004686)  
And a bigger item.

**[04:45:00.000] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004687)  
than all the budgets of health, agri, and social services put together.

**[04:45:08.280] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004688)  
Mr. Chair, Your Honor, if I can answer from a fiscal point of view,

**[04:45:13.320] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004689)  
which is why I am a strong advocate of fiscal consolidation.

**[04:45:17.000] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004690)  
When the administration started, the deficit to GDP was 7.3%.

**[04:45:25.000] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004691)  
We've narrowed that down to 6.2%, then 5.7%, last year 5.6%,

**[04:45:32.040] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004692)  
and this year we are trying to target 5.45% deficit to GDP.

**[04:45:37.220] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004693)  
Which means that we are becoming more efficient in collection of revenue.

**[04:45:42.640] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004694)  
And ideally, we start looking at our expenditure to spend smartly rather than volume.

**[04:45:52.580] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004695)  
It's the quality rather than the volume.

**[04:45:55.000] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004696)  
And I just want to point out that as far as expenditure goes,

**[04:46:01.380] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004697)  
if I compare to our regional neighbors, roughly, I'm oversimplifying the numbers,

**[04:46:06.760] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004698)  
but if our revenues are roughly 16% of GDP, we are at par or better than our neighbors.

**[04:46:15.160] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004699)  
However, our expenditure at 22% of GDP is much higher than our neighbors.

**[04:46:25.000] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004700)  
So, hence, we are creating a deficit,

**[04:46:28.700] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004701)  
which is why the economic team has created a fiscal framework, a plan, a path,

**[04:46:34.080] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004702)  
to keep reducing that fiscal deficit.

**[04:46:37.740] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004703)  
And as pointed out by my colleague earlier, these are already obligations of the government.

**[04:46:44.160] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004704)  
When the administration started, we had a total of 12.8 trillion pesos already in debt.

**[04:46:50.740] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004705)  
We had to start with that.

**[04:46:52.520] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004706)  
And we have obligations to...

**[04:46:55.000] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004707)  
to pay those.

**[04:46:58.220] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004708)  
And hence, we need to maintain our good credit rating globally,

**[04:47:04.560] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004709)  
which will allow us to borrow, continuously borrow, to fund priority programs of the government.

**[04:47:14.630] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004710)  
But, Secretary, since the brand of the budget for next year is a people-centered budget,

**[04:47:22.330] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004711)  
when can you start really using...

**[04:47:26.410] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004712)  
the higher levels of revenues of our economy?

**[04:47:30.630] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004713)  
For, first of all, the urgent recovery of the economy,

**[04:47:34.490] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004714)  
the infra and buffer stocking for Agri, high impact.

**[04:47:42.270] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004715)  
And then for the priority programs that are being called,

**[04:47:47.030] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004716)  
but ironically, for next year,

**[04:47:48.870] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004717)  
it was proposed that the health, Agri, and social services will be smaller.

**[04:47:55.490] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004718)  
And social services.

**[04:47:56.410] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004719)  
So, we can't recombine compared to the item for debt interest payments.

**[04:48:02.570] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004720)  
Even year-on-year, can't we adjust that to make the pesos and centavos really clearly more people-centered

**[04:48:11.490] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004721)  
while not completely letting go of our obligations to be good debtors?

**[04:48:17.490] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004722)  
Mr. Chair, Your Honor,

**[04:48:21.140] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004723)  
I believe that when we said that the budget is people-centered,

**[04:48:28.840] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004724)  
that means that the budget was very well scrutinized and chosen

**[04:48:32.160] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004725)  
so that the projects and programs that the government will implement

**[04:48:37.240] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004726)  
are those with the greatest multiplier effects,

**[04:48:40.800] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004727)  
well curated, and checked properly.

**[04:48:45.800] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004728)  
On your question of changing our debt obligations,

**[04:48:52.810] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004729)  
unfortunately, most...

**[04:48:53.710] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004730)  
Hindi naman po.

**[04:48:54.390] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004731)  
I recognize the debt obligations,

**[04:48:57.050] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004732)  
but doing a better balancing act of using yung sinabi nyo,

**[04:49:00.310] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004733)  
higher revenues natin,

**[04:49:02.570] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004734)  
vis-a-vis GDP as compared to our regional neighbors,

**[04:49:05.950] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004735)  
using those revenues more for the high-impact projects na pambawi sa economic downturn natin,

**[04:49:15.590] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004736)  
and then also for the developmental and social protection programs,

**[04:49:22.510] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004737)  
then parang priority kasi kung sa absolute numbers lang,

**[04:49:26.650] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004738)  
priority to pay yung debt interest,

**[04:49:30.310] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004739)  
rest obligations natin.

**[04:49:35.520] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004740)  
Mr. Chair, Your Honor,

**[04:49:36.660] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004741)  
I think the DBM is in a better position to explain the process of how they come up with the budget,

**[04:49:41.200] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004742)  
but I believe there are contractual obligations or automatic appropriations

**[04:49:49.700] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004743)  
that are always labeled first.

**[04:49:52.980] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004744)  
And I believe that interest payments, the NTA,

**[04:49:56.520] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004745)  
the NTA is even higher, Mr. Chair, Your Honor.

**[04:50:00.040] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004746)  
The interest payments are 1.1 trillion,

**[04:50:02.060] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004747)  
but the NTA is 1.3 trillion this year.

**[04:50:07.020] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004748)  
So all the automatic appropriations are allocated first,

**[04:50:13.060] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004749)  
if I may use that term.

**[04:50:14.840] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-004750)  
So it's an automatic appropriation, Mr. Chair, Your Honor.

**[04:50:20.400] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004751)  
I understand, Mr. Chair, Secretary,

**[04:50:22.880] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004752)  
and partly that's our historic problem about automatic appropriations.

**[04:50:27.980] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004753)  
But sige po, dumako tayo kay Sec de Leona.

**[04:50:31.060] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004754)  
I understand about...

**[04:50:32.060] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004755)  
how the budget is proposed to Congress.

**[04:50:35.320] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004756)  
But can you tell the committee better,

**[04:50:37.840] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004757)  
paano natin tatawagin pa rin itong people-centered budget,

**[04:50:42.260] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004758)  
given the way the proposed appropriations for the different items stack up

**[04:50:47.280] Senator Risa Hontiveros** (asr-004759)  
when compared to each other?

**[04:50:49.860] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004760)  
Mr. Chair, Your Honor,

**[04:50:52.120] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004761)  
well, as mentioned by the Secretary of Finance,

**[04:50:54.460] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004762)  
the premise why we are saying that the budget is still people-centered

**[04:50:58.060] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004763)  
is precisely because the biggest chunk of the budget

**[04:51:01.360] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004764)  
will still go to the people-centered budget.

**[04:51:01.920] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004765)  
It will still go to the social sector taken together.

**[04:51:04.740] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004766)  
And when we look at social sector,

**[04:51:07.000] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004767)  
it encompasses several different subsectors

**[04:51:11.040] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004768)  
from education, health, social security,

**[04:51:13.840] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004769)  
even housing and other social services.

**[04:51:17.000] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004770)  
And again, this sector receives the biggest chunk of the budget,

**[04:51:21.240] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004771)  
hence that we gave the priority to this sector.

**[04:51:25.180] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004772)  
But then again, if we compare it to our 2026 level,

**[04:51:29.080] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004773)  
there might be some nominal decrease,

**[04:51:31.920] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004774)  
precisely because of some inefficiencies encountered

**[04:51:34.540] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004775)  
by the implementing agencies for their current year's budget.

**[04:51:38.920] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004776)  
To name a few, Your Honor,

**[04:51:40.720] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004777)  
for health, HFEP, for agriculture, farm-to-market roads,

**[04:51:45.160] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004778)  
for DepEd classrooms,

**[04:51:46.920] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004779)  
all of these are infra which are not fully implemented

**[04:51:49.700] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004780)  
even at the middle of the year.

**[04:51:51.600] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004781)  
That's why this is a major consideration

**[04:51:53.380] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004782)  
while we have continued to provide budgets for these programs for 2027.

**[04:51:58.900] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004783)  
The amount is not at the same level

**[04:52:01.760] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004784)  
because...

**[04:52:01.920] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004785)  
Because precisely, the remaining balance by the end of this year

**[04:52:05.800] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004786)  
will have to be carried over for 2027.

**[04:52:09.180] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004787)  
One thing we'd also like to highlight, Mr. Chair, Your Honor,

**[04:52:12.400] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004788)  
is that for 2027, we tried to do some correcting measures

**[04:52:16.980] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004789)  
in terms of addressing some spending inefficiencies.

**[04:52:21.160] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004790)  
We noted during our presentation before we had lunch

**[04:52:25.820] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004791)  
that for the 2027 budget,

**[04:52:28.500] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004792)  
our revenue will be able,

**[04:52:31.920] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004793)  
to cover for PS and MOOE requirement,

**[04:52:35.200] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004794)  
which is not always the case in the previous year's budget.

**[04:52:39.000] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004795)  
So that actually raises some concern

**[04:52:41.460] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004796)  
on possible sustainability of implementing a budget

**[04:52:44.400] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004797)  
wherein we take on additional borrowings

**[04:52:47.100] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004798)  
and yet we just borrow for our regular operating requirements.

**[04:52:51.660] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004799)  
So at least the parameter that we use as the economic managers

**[04:52:55.400] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004800)  
is that if we resort to borrowings,

**[04:52:58.000] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004801)  
at least it will go to high-impact infrastructure

**[04:53:01.000] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004802)  
projects that will give us greater return

**[04:53:04.600] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004803)  
than the interest that we'll be paying eventually

**[04:53:07.620] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004804)  
to our creditors in the long term, Mr. Chair, Your Honor.

**[04:53:12.940] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004805)  
And Secretary De Leon,

**[04:53:15.840] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004806)  
so given nga yung automatic appropriations,

**[04:53:19.820] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004807)  
results also, especially in years like this one,

**[04:53:23.440] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004808)  
yung tighter fiscal space,

**[04:53:25.020] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004809)  
and yun na nga na-exceed nung interest payments,

**[04:53:30.080] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004810)  
yung...

**[04:53:30.840] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004811)  
budgets po together ng tatlong

**[04:53:32.700] Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon** (asr-004812)

**[05:57:57.460] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-006422)  
good governance,

**[05:57:59.460] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-006423)  
about

**[05:58:27.900] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-006426)

**[05:58:47.300] DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan** (asr-006427)

**[05:59:09.060] Senator Imee R. Marcos** (asr-006429)

**[05:59:53.620] Senator Imee R. Marcos** (asr-006432)

**[06:00:30.000] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-006439)  
The macroeconomic assumption of GDP growth of 5% to 6% is real GDP.

**[06:00:35.800] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-006440)  
And it also has an inflation factor of 4% to 5%.

**[06:00:39.660] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-006441)

**[06:00:44.340] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-006442)

**[06:00:48.480] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-006443)

**[06:00:58.760] Senator Imee R. Marcos** (asr-006446)

**[06:01:14.480] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-006449)

**[06:01:23.080] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-006450)

**[06:01:26.880] DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go** (asr-006451)

**[07:11:32.670] Senator Mark A. Villar** (asr-007692)

**[07:11:41.850] Senator Mark A. Villar** (asr-007693)

**[07:11:48.070] Senator Mark A. Villar** (asr-007694)
